Across five real-robot insertion tasks, PACE achieves an average success rate of 90.7%, outperforming vision-only and generation-time tactile-fusion baselines by over 44 percentage points; on the ManipulationNet benchmark, PACE maintains 88.7% success across six geometry-clearance configurations, including an industrial-grade 0.1-mm clearance. Ablations confirm the complementary contributions of the three temporal roles, mechanistic analyses show that PACE separates normal insertion progress from contact events requiring immediate correction, and cross-signal and cross-architecture experiments indicate that this temporal-role principle extends across different physical feedback signals and policy backbones. Videos and materials are available at https://pace-insertion.github.io/.

Robotics.title: ClothAtlas: Joint Garment Identification and State Estimation under Self-Occlusion
Robotics.summary: Garment manipulation requires inferring both garment identity and complete configuration from partial, self-occluded observations. This creates a chicken-and-egg problem: completing a partial observation requires a garment-specific deformation prior, while identifying the garment requires a configuration that explains the observation. We introduce ClothAtlas, which jointly identifies garments and estimates their complete configurations from partial point clouds and a library of canonical meshes. A shared graph-conditioned flow-matching model samples configurations for each candidate mesh and ranks candidates by observation fit. The model accommodates different mesh shapes, vertex counts, and connectivities, allowing new garments to be added from canonical meshes alone without retraining. On held-out DexGarmentLab garments, ClothAtlas ranks the correct mesh first among 221 candidates for all 22 test garments from a single flat observation. From a single self-occluded observation, it identifies 15/22 garments, compared with 8/22 for a deterministic graph estimator. Persistent vertex identities support grasp-target localization on real garments, reducing mean error from 15.4 to 6.4 cm overall and from 17.0 to 8.3 cm on occluded targets compared with dense descriptor matching. Project page: https://clothatlas.github.io/
Robotics.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Project page: https://clothatlas.github.io/

Robotics.title: Latent Telepathy: Multi-Robot Communication with Self-Supervised Perceptual Latents
Robotics.summary: In a decentralized multi-robot team under partial observability, the fact that decides a robot's next action is often visible only to a teammate. Existing decentralized methods communicate kinematic information, such as position or planned trajectory, which cannot convey what the teammate perceives. Learned communication in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) can carry perceptual content, but the resulting messages are task-coupled and opaque. We propose Latent Telepathy. Each robot broadcasts the perceptual latent vector it already computes for its own use, the output of an encoder trained with a self-supervised joint-embedding predictive objective, frozen, and shared across the team. A teammate learns to act on it from task reward alone. Because the encoder already runs for perception, the message costs no additional computation and a single compact vector of bandwidth. Because the encoder is frozen before any policy is trained, the message means the same thing to every robot, and the receiving robot is never told what it means. We evaluate Latent Telepathy with a content-controlled protocol in which bandwidth, latency, topology and receiver are held fixed and only the message content varies. Broadcasting the latent lets a navigator avoid an occluded hazard in 99.7% of episodes, matching a noiseless hand-designed message. Position and trajectory messages remain at chance, and the raw camera image, 186 times wider, is less reliable than the compressed latent. The result holds from a discrete gridworld to rendered pixels under continuous velocity control, and the encoder decodes the hazard from a physical robot's camera in 102 of 102 live decisions. We also identify a requirement for porting MARL communication results to continuous control, that the decision a message informs must remain reachable by exploration, and show how to restore it.
Robotics.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures. Submitted to IEEE ICRA 2027

Robotics.title: ProbeFlow: Training-Free Adaptive Flow Matching for Vision-Language-Action Models
Robotics.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies increasingly use Flow Matching (FM) action heads to generate action chunks as continuous trajectories. At inference, an FM head solves an ordinary differential equation (ODE): starting from a prior action latent, it repeatedly queries a learned velocity field to advance the state toward the decoded action chunk. Because each query depends on the preceding state, this iterative decoding can impose substantial sequential action-head cost at deployment. We propose ProbeFlow, a training-free framework that routes each action chunk to an integration schedule using a Lookahead Consistency Probe. Optional oscillation-conditioned (OSC) threshold adaptation reuses the same velocity evaluations and can trade part of the acceleration for potentially better task performance. On MetaWorld, the fixed-threshold configuration uses 2.60 scheduled steps (2.92 action-head evaluations) and reports 15.9 ms action-head latency, versus 235.7 ms for 50-step Euler, while obtaining 83.2% success versus 82.5%. On LIBERO, it uses 4.53 scheduled steps (5.09 action-head evaluations), reports 32.7 ms, and obtains 88.7% success, compared with 278.7 ms and 92.5% for 50-step Euler. We also evaluate OSC on three real-world manipulation tasks with 50 trials per method and task. These evaluations characterize action-decoding compute-performance trade-offs without additional training.

Robotics.title: Beyond Actions: Learning Future Operation Targets for Vision-Language-Action Models
Robotics.summary: Actions specify what a robot should execute, but do not describe what those commands will achieve. Vision-language-action (VLA) policies nevertheless learn primarily by predicting action chunks from images, language, and state. We introduce Action--Future Coupled Effect Learning (AFCE), which makes a future-grounded physical Effect the policy's primary prediction target. An offline tokenizer constructs temporally ordered Effect tokens from demonstrated actions, realized robot responses, and sparse visual transitions. Reconstruction objectives encourage the representation to retain executable detail and observed physical change. A flow-matching VLA predicts Effects from current images, instruction, and robot state, while a state-conditioned decoder converts them into action chunks. Embodiment-specific interfaces allow single- and dual-arm tasks to share the Effect model. On DexJoCo, AFCE achieves $50.97\%$ overall success, improving over $π_{0.5}$ and UVT by 11.82 and 15.21 percentage points, respectively. It leads on all five bimanual tasks, highlighting the value of Effect supervision for coordinated dexterous manipulation. The project page is available at https://afceproject.github.io/AFCE-Web/.

Robotics.title: DexJoCo-X: Benchmarking Action Representations for Multi-Hand Dexterous Manipulation
Robotics.summary: As dexterous hands proliferate, collecting data and training policies separately for every morphology becomes increasingly impractical. Scalable cross-embodiment learning therefore requires a unified representation that captures shared manipulation structure while preserving morphology-specific control. Differences in hands, tasks, datasets, and control interfaces prevent existing studies from isolating the effects of representation, pretraining, and architecture. We introduce DexJoCo-X, a benchmark and toolkit for controlled comparison across seven representative dexterous hands, six single-arm and bimanual tasks, and 2,100 balanced demonstrations. DexJoCo-X provides a matched multi-hand, multi-task protocol with common scenes, success criteria, and execution interfaces, redesigned glove-to-hand mappings, and an automated pipeline that expands reviewed demonstrations across randomized scenes. Using $π_{0.5}$, Ego-Pi, and Being-H0.5, we examine whether a shared action interface is sufficient for multi-hand learning. Expanding $π_{0.5}$ to an 80-dimensional bimanual output yields near-zero success. Ego-Pi preserves the pretrained action head through interleaved prediction and supports per-hand multi-task learning, but remains ineffective for seven-hand joint training. By contrast, Being-H0.5 combines cross-embodiment pretraining, a unified action space, and embodiment-aware experts, enabling one policy to control all seven hands. Within this architecture, function-aligned action slots achieve 47.7% mean success, compared with 47.0% for native coordinates and 33.1% for DexLatent. These results show that cross-embodiment representation depends on the entire learning system: action coordinates, pretraining, and architecture must jointly separate shared manipulation structure from embodiment-specific control.
Robotics.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Updated photography illustrations in Fig. 2; text and results unchanged. Project website: https://jxw-wei.github.io/DexJoCo-X-website/

Robotics.title: Invariant Stochastic Filtering on SE(3) for Inertial-Encoder State Estimation of Serial Rigid Manipulators
Robotics.summary: An invariant extended Kalman filter (IEKF) is developed for state estimation of serial rigid manipulators with an arbitrary number of links, formulated entirely within the Lie group $SE(3)$. The group-affine property of the kinematic equations makes the linearised error dynamics autonomous, so the Riccati equation governs the true error covariance rather than a local approximation. A physically separated noise model treats gyroscope and accelerometer channels independently: the accelerometer provides translational twist via gravity-compensated integration, yielding a measurement covariance that scales with the sample interval in exact analogy with process noise discretisation; a state-dependent Coriolis noise term captures gyroscope noise propagating through the nonlinear dynamics, vanishing at rest and growing with twist magnitude. The filter is structured as a modular chain of per-link IEKFs in which the predicted covariance of each link depends on its predecessor only through the Adjoint-transformed posterior, giving linear computational cost in link count. Exponential ultimate boundedness in mean square is established via a Lie algebra Lyapunov function, with per-link bounds chained through the Adjoint operator norm to yield a stability certificate that is modular and scalable to arbitrary chain length. The state is augmented with gyroscope biases without loss of the autonomous error dynamics or the modular structure. The design is validated in a three-dimensional simulation of a two-link chain with encoder and IMU fusion, in a software-in-the-loop study of an industrial hydraulic rammer-boom manipulator in which the encoder row is replaced by a gravity-referenced virtual encoder for IMU-only estimation.
Robotics.comment: This document is an arXiv preprint posted for open access and citation purposes. It is under review and subject to revision

Robotics.title: Graph3R: Unifying View Graph Initialization with Feed-Forward Reconstruction
Robotics.summary: Feed-forward reconstruction recovers camera poses and dense geometry from image sets whose views are assumed to come from a single scene. In practice, uncurated image collections often contain views from disjoint scenes, and reconstructing these views jointly can corrupt camera poses and geometry. Existing pipelines typically resolve view associations in separate stages before final reconstruction, leaving view graph initialization and reconstruction inference only loosely coupled. We introduce Graph3R, which unifies view graph initialization with feed-forward reconstruction through a shared geometric representation. A lightweight verification head predicts pairwise covisibility from the multi-view features of $π^3$ to construct a view graph. This graph classifies the input views into scene groups. For each group, we mask the shared features before decoding camera poses and dense geometry. Reusing the multi-view features allows Graph3R to reconstruct disjoint scenes separately with a single backbone pass. Across three benchmarks, Graph3R improves average maximum recall at 100% precision by upto 8.99 percentage points over the baseline, while improving reconstruction quality on mixed-scene inputs. Regarding the multi-session mapping task, Graph3R improves cross-session localization and achieves competitive pose estimation accuracy, while delivering a runtime speedup of approximately $35.9\times$ over the baseline when reconstructing the query group. By integrating learned view association with geometric inference, our approach takes a step toward end-to-end reconstruction from uncurated image collections.

Robotics.title: Same Goal, Different Words: Spatial Instruction Sensitivity in World-Action Models
Robotics.summary: World-action models should preserve the intended manipulation across equivalent descriptions of a spatial goal. We evaluate this consistency in 864 rollouts from three models across four RoboLab scenes, holding initial states and task goals fixed. Describing relations through the reference object rather than the object-to-move lowers the rate of reaching a stable placement by 12.2 percentage points on average. The effect of instruction rephrasing varies across spatial relations, so aggregate scores can hide sensitivity to wording. Standalone tests of the policies' language understanding identify relation reversals and show that adding images can disrupt otherwise correct text-only interpretations. Rollout analysis also distinguishes spatial placement from instruction following: moving the wrong object can satisfy the requested relation, and rates of stable placement fall from 43.2% at any time to 21.8% at episode end. These findings motivate a more thorough evaluation of world-action models' steerability, language understanding, and grounding. Evaluations should test consistency across equivalent instructions, verify that the intended object moved, and check whether the requested arrangement persists to the end of the rollout.

Robotics.title: Embodied Skill Bench: Benchmarking How Well Agents with Embodied Skills Perform on Physical Tasks
Robotics.summary: LLM agents increasingly control robots using VLA policies, perception models, and procedural knowledge. These modules are difficult to reuse because their interfaces, embodiment assumptions, and conditions of use differ, and their benefits on physical tasks remain unclear. We package them as embodied skills that extend agent skills with explicit embodiment assumptions and conditions of use, building 250 action, perception, and experience skills from 1,052 resources. On this basis we introduce EmbodiedSkillBench, which runs an agent in a closed observation-action loop and records success, actions, tokens, and wall-clock time. It supports three modes: native control, skill-only execution, and Agent-Directed Reuse (ADR), a mode we propose in which the agent keeps its native controls and decides for each skill whether to invoke, modify, or ignore it. Across four agents on 100 perturbed LIBERO-Pro tasks, we find that skills help an agent only as far as they exceed what it can already do. Skill-only execution lifts GPT-5.6-Sol from 11% to 63% and Kimi-K3 and Claude-Opus-5 by about 20 points, while cutting their token usage by 58% to 85%. Yet all four agents then end up between 61% and 64%, and GPT-6-Astra falls from 92% under native control to 61%. This suggests that as agents grow stronger, the role of embodied skills shifts from supplying missing capability to reducing cost: GPT-6-Astra already solves most tasks through native control, so restricting it to skills removes more than it adds. Under ADR, which lets it keep native control and call skills selectively, GPT-6-Astra recovers to 85%, within 7 points of native control, while using 14.1% fewer tokens and 11.9% less time. With Jev as a skill choosing motion directions and gripper actions, it reaches 81% with 50% fewer tokens and 57% less time. The code is available at https://github.com/HanZhi306/EmbodiedSkill-Bench.
Robotics.comment: 25 pages, 7 figures, 9 tables, including appendices. Code: https://github.com/HanZhi306/EmbodiedSkill-Bench

Robotics.title: MSC: Multi-Stage Caster-aware Control Framework with Uncertainty-Aware NMPC and RL-based Execution Layer
Robotics.summary: Freely swiveling casters are widely adopted in industrial AMRs/SDVs for their mechanical simplicity and load capacity. However, caster misalignment during low-speed or high-curvature maneuvers induces strong contact nonlinearities, widening the planning-execution gap between commanded $(v, ω)$ and realized motion. Existing caster-aware strategies are highly sensitive to state-estimation reliability, causing unstable execution in uncertain transition regimes. To address this, we present Multi-Stage Caster-aware Control (MSC), a planning-execution integrated hierarchical framework featuring two core mechanisms. First, an uncertainty-aware NMPC (CU-MPC) dynamically schedules caster-aware costs and input regularization using predictive uncertainty to suppress overly aggressive maneuvers. Second, a reinforcement learning-based execution layer estimates and predicts caster states under partial observability, transforming high-level velocity commands into physically executable wheel speeds adapted to current contact conditions. Validations in Isaac Sim and real robots demonstrate that MSC offers a clear comparative advantage over existing decoupled compensation approaches by significantly improving caster-state estimation accuracy, minimizing misalignment, and enhancing tracking robustness in caster-sensitive maneuvers.

Robotics.title: One-Shot Learning for Double-Shot Latte Art: Adapting Cobot Pouring Skills with Dynamic Movement Primitives
Robotics.summary: Latte art is a complex task requiring dexterity and precision, making it a challenging and commercially relevant task. A one-shot learning system is employed in which a single barista demonstration is segmented into five functionally distinct phases, each encoded as an independent Cartesian Dynamic Movement Primitive (CDMP) with its own parameters. Against a single-CDMP baseline, per-phase encoding reduces transition endpoint error by 3.2-4.5 times and art-stroke shape error by 2.7 times, reproducing jug tilt to below 1 degree RMS in the pouring phases. The learnt pour scales from a 280mL to a 400mL cup through a single spatial offset and a scaled recipe, with no re-demonstration. The phase-based CDMP approach generalises beyond latte art to any demonstration task whose phases have distinct spatial or temporal requirements whilst demonstrating the ability to adapt reproductions to suit different task requirements.

Robotics.title: Extending Wire-Driven Parallel Robots to Multi-Floating-Link Systems with an Inter-Body Wire
Robotics.summary: Parallel wire-driven systems are a framework in which multiple wires are connected to an end effector, and the end effector is driven by the tensions of those wires. Because they can transmit large forces, up to the breaking strength of the wires, over lengths on the order of several tens of meters, they can realize powerful actuation in large workspaces. In recent years, studies have also investigated connecting wires to external environments such as trees and columns and forming parallel wire actuation on site. However, conventional parallel wire-driven systems often assume a single end effector, and because of interference between wires and links in a shared workspace, it has been difficult to handle multiple floating links simultaneously. In this study, we realize multi-floating-link parallel wire actuation by introducing an inter-body wire. In real-robot experiments, the two bodies supported and lifted a mannequin and transferred it onto a stretcher as a rescue motion. This shows that parallel wire actuation can be extended from a single end effector to a multi-floating-link system, and indicates its potential for broader tasks such as the manipulation of large objects and rescue support.
Robotics.comment: Accepted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, website: https://shin0805.github.io/twinx_multi_floating_link/

Robotics.title: SERF: Spatiotemporal Environment and Robot Feature Map for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation
Robotics.summary: Long-horizon robot mobile manipulation requires continual reasoning about localization, environment changes, and task progress, all of which are challenging to infer from image observations alone. In this paper, we show that conditioning a mobile manipulation policy on a spatiotemporal feature map improves reasoning over long horizons. The map represents the environment and the articulated robot body as neural points in a shared latent space and is updated online from egocentric observations and proprioceptive state. We update the environment neural points using object-level rigid tracking and the robot neural points using forward kinematics. We use our spatiotemporal environment and robot feature (SERF) map as a state input to a vision-language-action (VLA) model by extracting map tokens from multiple reference frames and spatial scales, providing the policy with both local and global context. We demonstrate SERF on BEHAVIOR-1K, a benchmark for long-horizon mobile manipulation in household environments. Experiments show that the SERF VLA policy outperforms image-only baselines, reaches subgoals faster by following more direct trajectories, improves robustness to scene-configuration shifts, and recovers from object-drop failures.

Robotics.title: FlowVLA: Enabling World Dynamics Understanding through Pluggable 3D Flow Learning
Robotics.summary: Recent advances in 3D reconstruction enable the extraction of temporally consistent 3D motion from RGB observations; however, current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models still predominantly rely on 2D image-text priors. Therefore, they do not accurately represent the fundamental dynamics of the 3D world associated with physical actions. This over-reliance on static 2D visual cues limits the capacity of VLA models in achieving robust robot manipulation. To address these limitations, we introduce FlowVLA, a reconstruction-guided, pluggable 3D flow learning framework aimed at empowering VLA models with an inherent understanding of action-relevant dynamics. Instead of requiring explicit 3D sensor inputs or altering the inference-time architecture, our method is designed to utilize temporally aligned 3D flow only during training. This allows the model to learn the dynamic evolution of the physical scene while preserving the computational efficiency of conventional 2D VLA backbones. To bridge scene-level dynamics with robotic manipulation, we propose a modular 3D flow learning framework with dual-level flow supervision. Specifically, point-level flow guides the model to forecast the future displacements of task-critical 3D points, while TCP-level flow aggregates these motions to align with the robot's TCP trajectories. This dual-level flow supervision encourages the model to focus on semantically meaningful dynamic regions, effectively coupling scene-level motion with precise control signals. Extensive evaluations across simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate that FlowVLA consistently improves manipulation performance, zero-shot robustness, and optimizes data efficiency. FlowVLA adds only lightweight auxiliary heads during training and discards them at inference. Therefore, FlowVLA introduces no additional 3D sensor inputs, architectural modifications, or inference-time computation.
Robotics.comment: 20 pages, 16 figures. Accepted at Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) 2026

Robotics.title: ActMem-VLA: Action-History Memory with Dual-Expert Denoising for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Policies
Robotics.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have driven rapid progress in robotic manipulation, demonstrating strong fine-grained control and promising performance on long-horizon tasks. However, many existing VLAs lack explicit access to interaction history, making them vulnerable to perceptual aliasing: similar current observations and robot states at different task stages may induce action ambiguity and lower success rate. Existing methods incorporate temporal or progress cues through feature conditioning, action-prior modification, or sampling guidance. However, methods that jointly fine-tune memory modules and the base VLA incur additional policy-training costs, motivating the separation of trainable history-conditioned steering from frozen base-policy refinement. We propose ActMem-VLA, a dual-expert handover architecture that augments a frozen, fine-tuned VLA with a memory plugin comprising a Mamba-based memory module and a lightweight PreAction Expert (PAE). Specifically, Mamba encodes executed-action history into memory that conditions PAE alongside current context. With these inputs, PAE steers task progression during early, high-noise denoising, then passes the partially denoised action to the frozen Action Expert (AE) to refine action details during the remaining low-noise steps. The fine-tuned base VLA remains frozen throughout training, while only the Mamba module and PAE are jointly optimized. On LIBERO-Mem, ActMem-VLA achieves 80.8\% average success across all ten tasks, compared with 65.2\% for $π_{0.5}$ and 49.5\% for MemoryVLA, while introducing only 3.45\% additional parameters. Across four real-world tasks, it improves the average success rate over $π_{0.5}$ by 28.8\%.

Robotics.title: Directional Pullback Regularization for Long-Horizon Rollout of Latent World Models in Autonomous Driving
Robotics.summary: Learned world models for autonomous driving operate in unconstrained latent spaces, yet the physical systems they represent are governed by strict non-holonomic constraints: ground vehicles cannot realize instantaneous pure lateral motion. We study long-horizon latent rollout modeling for autonomous driving and ask whether rollout quality can be improved by assigning a motion-aware geometry to latent transitions, rather than by redesigning the predictor architecture. Starting from an unconstrained latent rollout baseline, we introduce Directional Pullback Regularization (DPR), a training time method that defines a kinematics-aware anisotropic Riemannian metric in decoded state space and pulls it back through the decoder Jacobian to the latent manifold. The resulting latent-space metric assigns higher cost to latent directions that decode to lateral vehicle motion, while preserving the original encoder-dynamics-decoder backbone. This yields a clean three-way comparison among an Unconstrained Latent Rollout model (ULR), an Euclidean Pullback Regularization ablation (EPR), and the full directional method (DPR). We evaluate all models on open-loop ego-motion rollout over a common 10-second test horizon, using training rollout lengths of 1, 3, 5, and 10 steps. Across all four training regimes, DPR achieves lower 10-second final displacement error than both ULR and EPR. The strongest relative accuracy gain appears for models trained with 3-step rollout supervision, where DPR reduces the 10-second final displacement error by approximately 44 percent relative to ULR. The strongest overall control-relevant tradeoff is obtained for longer rollout-trained models, especially at 10 steps, where DPR simultaneously improves displacement error, lateral motion consistency, and forward motion preservation relative to both ULR and EPR.

Robotics.title: Event-Based Visual Teach-and-Repeat via Fast Fourier-Domain Cross-Correlation
Robotics.summary: Visual teach-and-repeat (VT&R) navigation enables robots to autonomously traverse previously demonstrated paths using visual feedback. We present a novel event-camera-based VT&R system. Our system formulates event-stream matching as frequency-domain cross-correlation, transforming spatial convolutions into efficient Fourier-space multiplications. By exploiting the binary structure of event frames and applying image compression techniques, we achieve a processing latency of just 2.88 ms, about 3.5 times faster than conventional camera-based baselines that are optimised for runtime efficiency. Experiments using a Prophesee EVK4 HD event camera mounted on an AgileX Scout Mini robot demonstrate successful autonomous navigation across 3000+ meters of indoor and outdoor trajectories in daytime and nighttime conditions. Our system maintains Cross-Track Errors (XTE) below 15 cm, demonstrating the practical viability of event-based perception for real-time VT&R navigation.
Robotics.comment: 8 Pages, 5 Figures, paper accepted to the 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS 2026)

Robotics.title: Constrained Differentiable Policy Learning for Safe Quadrotor Navigation
Robotics.summary: Differentiable simulation enables efficient policy optimization through analytic gradients, yet safety is commonly incorporated as a weighted penalty, requiring manual tuning of the trade-off between task performance and constraint satisfaction. We instead formulate obstacle avoidance as an explicit constraint and train quadrotor policies using primal--dual gradient descent--ascent through a differentiable simulator. We introduce two key components to enable effective constrained training. First, we propose a bounded clearance-based constraint function that provides informative gradients around the safety boundary while preventing large violations from destabilizing primal--dual optimization. Second, we introduce log-mean-exp (LME) aggregation to smoothly emphasize critical per-step safety violations across a trajectory and training batch within a single constraint governed by one dual variable. Together, these components enable the desired safety level to be specified directly while balancing constraint satisfaction and task completion. We theoretically prove that the proposed optimization with differentiable simulation converges to feasible policy under mild assumptions. Experiments demonstrate improved safety--performance trade-offs over fixed-penalty and existing policy-learning baselines, as well as generalization to denser out-of-distribution environments. Finally, the learned policy transfers zero-shot to Gazebo/PX4 and a physical quadrotor without additional fine-tuning.

Robotics.title: HWAM: Humanoid World Action Model With Joint State--Action Generation
Robotics.summary: Humanoid robots are a promising platform for general-purpose manipulation. Recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies learn actions directly from multimodal observations, while World Action Models (WAMs) further incorporate future visual prediction to improve action generation. However, in hierarchical humanoid systems, VLA and WAM policies output reference actions that are subsequently realized through whole-body control, robot dynamics, balance, and contact. This hierarchy creates an action--execution gap: the reference produced by the policy can differ from the motion realized by the robot. Without explicitly modeling the realized body state, future visual prediction must jointly explain scene evolution and discrepancies between reference actions and executed motion, making it difficult to associate an action with its physical outcome. We propose HWAM, a Humanoid World Action Model with joint state--action generation, which makes the robot's post-execution proprioceptive state an explicit prediction target. By jointly generating reference actions and their realized body states, HWAM directly incorporates supervision of executed motion into action learning. HWAM is trained through three complementary conditional paths. The Policy path jointly denoises state--action trajectories conditioned only on current observations, matching deployment conditions. Forward Dynamics Modeling (FDM) predicts future visual observations conditioned on actions and post-execution states, while Inverse Dynamics Modeling (IDM) reconstructs the joint trajectory from visual transitions. Together, these paths connect policy references, realized body motion, and visual outcomes. HWAM achieves the highest success rate among evaluated baselines on three real-robot tasks on the LimX OLI humanoid. On Candy Picking, HWAM achieves a 70.6% success rate, compared with 43.3% for Fast-WAM.

Robotics.title: PathLift: Depth-Conditioned Metric Lifting for Visual-Navigation Priors
Robotics.summary:
Generalist visual-navigation policies tell a robot which direction to go but not how far. A separate lifting step is needed at deployment to convert their unitless trajectory into a metric path that a controller can track; existing scalar lifters apply uniform scaling that misses per-waypoint corrections, while in-policy approaches that inject monocular depth into the policy inherit the prediction errors of the depth model near obstacles and at close range.
  We present PathLift, a per-waypoint depth-conditioned adapter that lifts a pre-trained visual-navigation policy by consuming an explicit, sensor-grade depth source (RGB-D, stereo, or projected LiDAR) and fitting per-waypoint magnitude and lateral residuals to a canonicalized prior.
  PathLift consistently improves closed-loop navigation across diverse visual-navigation policies in simulation and on a real wheeled robot under both stereo and LiDAR depth. By turning the policy's unitless intent into a depth-feasible metric path in a single feed-forward pass, the adapter lifts real-world success without test-time optimization.
Robotics.comment: 9 pages of main text, accepted to CoRL 2026

Robotics.title: Simultaneous Forward and Inverse Human-in-the-Loop Optimization
Robotics.summary: Subjective user experience is important to human-robot interaction, but the outcomes users value, and how those preferences vary across individuals and contexts, are often unknown. While inverse learning approaches using human data can help identify user rewards, in many assistive settings the experimental costs of executing a control policy, measuring biomechanical or physiological outcomes, and collecting user feedback often limit the number of queries and optimization iterations. Here, we present Simultaneous Forward and Inverse Human-In-the-Loop Optimization (SFIHILO), which efficiently infers individual-specific reward functions from preferences over human outcomes and identifies a final control policy that maximizes the learned reward. SFIHILO bootstraps a forward model to predict user outcomes from control policies, uses this model for active querying to accelerate inverse reward learning, and then optimizes the final control policy without additional user trials. We score candidate policies by their expected reduction in uncertainty across both forward and inverse beliefs, targeting a regional preference boundary to robustly inform this simultaneous learning process. In simulation, we show that SFIHILO was effective across user heterogeneity, outcome dimensionalities, precision requirements, noise levels, and nonstationarity; compared with mutual information approaches, the proposed active querying strategy significantly improved sample efficiency in inverse learning while preserving forward model accuracy. This approach demonstrates the potential to infer latent human goals, enabling more transferable and effective human-robot interaction.
Robotics.comment: Accepted at the 10th Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026)

Robotics.title: Why Learning Rediscovers the Closed-Form Diagonal Regularizer
Robotics.summary: Recovering modal amplitudes from a few sensors requires regularization, and the shape of the penalty decides how strongly each mode is shrunk. The best shape depends on the truncation noise that discarded modes add to every measurement, which is unobserved and could be room-specific. We identify a diagonal saturation principle: for a single snapshot, isotropic truncation noise makes the Bayes-optimal Tikhonov shape a closed-form power law Gamma_k proportional to lambda_k^|s|, set by the prior alone and independent of the domain. The off-diagonal anisotropy equals the Herfindahl index H of the discarded-mode power exactly, Weyl's eigenvalue counting law fixes the number of discarded modes and hence H, and Berry's random-wave conjecture enters only through a diagonal term D, which we measure directly. Together they predict an approximately flat loss landscape over the penalty exponent, which leaves a learned diagonal regularizer little to gain from tuning the exponent per room. On simulated acoustic rooms the closed form stays within 5.83% of a per-room power-law oracle across observation windows, and three learned diagonal architectures track its error, the closest within a fraction of a point and none more than 3pp above it, while learning qualitatively different spectra. In the truncation regime no tested method consistently improves on the closed form, including Learned Iterative Ridge, which couples modes across layers. The framework extends to heat diffusion through a known Green's-function correction with no new free parameters.

Robotics.title: SemAnCorr: Semantic Anchored Correspondence for Zero-Shot Manipulation Skill Transfer
Robotics.summary: Transferring manipulation skills across object instances that share functionality but differ in geometry remains a fundamental challenge in robot learning. While recent correspondence methods leverage dense visual descriptors and 3D feature fields, nearest-neighbor feature matching often produces spatially incoherent correspondences that fail to recover the local geometric frames required for reliable skill transfer. We introduce SemAnCorr, a training-free framework that establishes dense correspondence by selecting semantically consistent anchor regions through joint pose-correspondence optimization and propagating these constraints over the object surface using functional maps. The resulting correspondences preserve both semantic consistency and geometric coherence, enabling object-centric manipulation skills to transfer across geometrically diverse instances. We evaluate SemAnCorr on a dense correspondence benchmark built on PartNet-Mobility, achieving 90.8% semantic accuracy in our benchmark evaluation while improving geometric coherence over recent state-of-the-art baselines. Finally, we show that these improvements translate directly into real-world manipulation performance: using a single demonstration, SemAnCorr enables substantially more reliable zero-shot manipulation skill transfer to previously unseen objects than existing correspondence methods. Videos and additional visualizations are available at https://semancorr.github.io .

Robotics.title: SIMPLE: Simulation-Based Policy Learning and Evaluation for Humanoid Loco-manipulation
Robotics.summary: Humanoid foundation models are advancing faster than we can evaluate them. While real-world testing is expensive and difficult to reproduce, existing simulation benchmarks focus primarily on table-top or wheeled robots. A scalable and reproducible benchmark for whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation remains an open problem. To this end, we present SIMPLE, a unified simulation testbed for humanoid policy learning and evaluation. SIMPLE couples the accurate contact-rich dynamics of MuJoCo with the photorealistic rendering of IsaacSim. It provides a large-scale environment comprising 16 diverse whole-body tasks, 50 indoor scenes, and over 1,000 object assets. To facilitate scalable data collection, the framework integrates two data generation pipelines: automated trajectory generation via motion planning and a low-latency VR teleoperation interface. We further integrate and benchmark mainstream humanoid policies at scale in SIMPLE, including lightweight imitation networks, large vision-language-action (VLA) models, and recent world action models (WAMs). Our experiments reveal a strong correlation between policy performance in simulation and the real world. Furthermore, we demonstrate that policies trained on data collected in SIMPLE can be transferred zero-shot to physical humanoid robots under similar settings, providing a robust and reproducible foundation for humanoid robotics research.

Optimization and Control.title: Fundamental Limits of Prescribed-Time Regulation: Gain Budgets, Accuracy Frontiers, and Arrival Costs
Optimization and Control.summary: Prescribed-time controllers drive the state to the origin at a time $T$ chosen in advance, with gains that grow without bound as $t$ approaches $T$. This paper shows the growth is a necessity and computes the exact price of avoiding it. The starting point is a simple estimate: any trajectory with $\|\dot z(t)\|\le L(t)\|z(t)\|$ satisfies $\|z(t)\|\ge\|z(0)\|e^{-\int_0^t L}$. From this: a gain profile $L$ supports exact prescribed-time convergence, over the unrestricted class of closed-loop vector fields admitting it, if and only if its integral over $[0,T)$ is infinite; so every design must either use an envelope of infinite integral or violate the linear growth bound at the origin, as finite-time and fixed-time designs do. Under a finite gain budget $\mathcal B=\int_0^T L$ the best worst-case contraction over the class is exactly $e^{-\mathcal B}$, a floor valid for every plant, and a finite-budget trajectory converges to a definite point away from the origin. A comparison lemma then carries the theory beyond linear growth: for envelopes $\|\dot z\|\le L(t)\,ω(\|z\|)$, first arrival at the origin requires budget at least $\int_0^{\|z_0\|}du/ω(u)$; arrival is impossible whenever this integral diverges, and when it is finite it is the exact threshold, attained inside the class. The classical settling expressions of finite-time control reappear as hitting-time floors, and the known fixed-time condition is the two-ended convergence of the same integral. For linear time-varying loops the results refine to logarithmic-norm budgets, corollaries of a known two-sided estimate, with the terminal error of gain freezing described exactly.

Optimization and Control.title: Balancing cost and demand in a smart grid - a mean-field game analysis
Optimization and Control.summary: In a smart grid, consumers can also play the role of producers and sellers of energy. Therefore, the control of a smart grid over time becomes a dynamic game with a large number of small players and one or several large players. This is much more complicated than the control of an energy system with a single producer. The framework of mean-field games with common noise allows the transformation of such a complicated model into a control problem for a typical prosumer (producer and consumer in one) optimizing his behavior against a flow of other such prosumers. In our model, we introduce 2 decision variables for such a controller: one describing the amount of electric energy bought from the grid (or sold to it), and the second one describing the charging rate for our battery. The cost function is designed to satisfy two goals: satisfying the demand of the consumer (a single home) and minimizing the payment for energy. Players are allowed to sell/buy energy from the grid. Common noise is hidden in price volatility and sun irradiance, which influence all the players. We compute the optimal controls for our model and simulate solutions on real data. The novelty of our construction, compared to other works on smart grid control, lies in combining the minimization of the cost of energy and sustaining some level of demand satisfaction. We analyze the impact of battery usage on achieving a balance between these two criteria. We also take into account that the smart grid is only part of the energy market, which makes consumer strategies dependent on energy consumption outside the grid.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal Feature-Based Newsvendor Policies under Censored Demand
Optimization and Control.summary: We investigate a newsvendor problem where a decision-maker observes a $z$-dimensional vector of covariates, and wants to learn how much stock to order given a sample of size $n$ of censored demand data to minimize costs. Demand is censored when insufficient stock is available to meet it, and past stocking quantities are known. We propose a new model-agnostic loss function approach to estimate optimal order quantities using observational data, and characterize the optimal newsvendor policy as the policy that minimizes our proposed loss function. Our method requires only a single estimation step, can be scaled to datasets with hundreds of thousands of data points, and does not suffer from the same instabilities as inverse censoring probability weighting methods. We describe how this loss function can be implemented in linear empirical risk minimization, kernel weights optimization and deep neural network algorithms, and provide excess risk generalization bounds for their out-of-sample performance. Moreover, we show through numerical experiments that our method quickly converges to the optimal policy on synthetic data, and leads to improved performance on real world retail data.

Optimization and Control.title: Spectral Self-Concordant Barriers: A Proof of a Conjecture by Tunçel
Optimization and Control.summary: Let $Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a open, convex, and symmetric set and let $f:Q \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a $\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier function, that is also symmetric. We show the associated spectral function $F(X)= \mathcal{O}^2 (f \circ λ)(X)$ is a $\mathcal{O}^2\vartheta$-self-concordant function, where $\mathcal{O} = 8\max\{1+3\vartheta, 12\}$, on the domain of all $n \times n$ symmetric matrices $X$, with eigenvalues $λ(X) \in Q$. This generalizes the relationship between the standard logarithmic barriers $-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i$ and $-\log \det X$ and gives a solution to a conjecture by L.~Tunçel, 1995.

Optimization and Control.title: Tight semidefinite programming relaxations for sparse box-constrained quadratic programs
Optimization and Control.summary: We introduce a new class of semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations for sparse box-constrained quadratic programs, obtained by a novel integration of the Reformulation Linearization Technique into standard SDP relaxations while explicitly exploiting the sparsity of the problem. The resulting relaxations are not implied by some of the most widely-used LP and SDP relaxations for this class of optimization problems. We establish a sufficient condition under which the convex hull of the feasible region of the lifted quadratic program is SDP-representable; the proof is constructive and yields an explicit extended formulation. Although the resulting SDP may be of exponential size in general, we further identify additional structural conditions on the sparsity of the optimization problem that guarantee the existence of a polynomial-size SDP-representable formulation, which can be constructed in polynomial time.

Optimization and Control.title: (Approximate) Symmetric Extension Complexity of the Spanning Tree Polytope
Optimization and Control.summary:
We prove a tight lower bound on symmetric LP formulations for the spanning tree polytope of the complete graph. More precisely, let $P_{ST}(K_n)$ be the spanning tree polytope of $K_n$. We show that, for all $n\ge13$, every symmetric extended formulation for $P_{ST}(K_n)$ has at least $\binom n3$ inequalities. Since the classical Martin formulation has a symmetric formulation of size $O(n^3)$, this gives \[
  \operatorname{xcs}(P_{ST}(K_n))=Θ(n^3). \] We also study outer relaxations of the spanning tree polytope of $K_n$ for maximization with nonnegative edge weights. We show that for every fixed approximation factor below $3/2$, symmetric LP formulations still require $Θ(n^3)$ inequalities for all sufficiently large $n$, whereas factor $3/2$ admits a formulation of size $O(n^2)$. Moreover, we provide an exact symmetric SDP formulation of size $O(n^2)$, measured by PSD matrix order, which implies $\operatorname{xc}_{\mathrm{psd}}(P_{ST}(K_n))= Θ(n^2)$. Thus symmetric LP and SDP sizes already differ for exact formulations, and for every fixed approximation factor $1\leβ<3/2$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
Optimization and Control.comment: Added results on approximate LP formulations and exact SDP formulations

Optimization and Control.title: A Controlled Null Result for Per-Gate Riemannian Optimization in VQE
Optimization and Control.summary: Parametrized gates in a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) live on a product of unitary groups, which makes Riemannian optimization a natural candidate for improving training. We test this candidate in the clean per-gate setting: each single-qubit gate is optimized directly on U (2) and compared with Adam on an unconstrained Euler-angle chart representing the same physical gate, initialized from the same unitaries and tuned with a separate learning-rate sweep. On a validated hydrogen-chain benchmark, we find no measurable practical advantage from the Riemannian machinery. The direct manifold optimizer and the Euler-coordinate baseline are interleaved in final error and success rate; the classical coordinate baseline is not slower in iterations on the successful cells; and the choices of Riemannian metric, retraction, and momentum vector transport do not change the conclusion. We also identify four failure modes that can manufacture an apparent positive result: a trivial product-state benchmark, a projected-matrix Adam baseline that discards most of its own step, a non-unitary inherited Cayley retraction that lets the reported energy pass below the variational minimum, and a learning-rate grid whose optimum sits at its boundary. Each failure mode produced a plausible multi-seed result in our own workflow before being caught. The practical output of this paper is therefore a controlled null result and a validation checklist for VQE optimizer comparisons.

Optimization and Control.title: Beyond periodicity: Fourier methods for optimal control
Optimization and Control.summary: Fourier-based spectral methods provide compact global approximations, permit simple differentiation and integration, and achieve spectral convergence for smooth periodic functions. Their use in finite-horizon optimal control problems (OCPs) is nevertheless challenged by the generally nonperiodic state and control trajectories: endpoint mismatch induces artificial discontinuities and can destroy spectral convergence. Leveraging Eckhoff-type endpoint-correction techniques, we develop a Fourier-based spectral framework for OCPs with possibly nonlinear dynamics and constraints. The correction improves convergence without enlarging the set of decision variables, yielding an efficient finite-dimensional numerical method. Furthermore, we formulate selected dynamics and obstacle-avoidance constraints through Sobolev residual bounds, which incorporate information about the residuals over the entire time horizon and improve constraint satisfaction. Numerical experiments on benchmark problems demonstrate competitive computational performance, lower residual errors, and improved solution accuracy.

Optimization and Control.title: Proof of Stake economy under centralized exchanges--a mean field model
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider the interaction between centralized trading and decentralized Proof of Stake (PoS) blockchain ecosystems. Motivated by the increasing dominance of centralized exchanges and the institutionalization of crypto markets, we study how trading activities on centralized exchanges affect staking behavior, token allocation, and decentralization within a PoS blockchain. We formulate a continuous-time mean field model, where the miners simultaneously act as validators in the PoS protocol and traders in a centralized market with price impact. Under suitable assumptions, we establish the local well-posedness of the mean field system, and derive a semi-explicit characterization of the equilibrium trading strategy. Numerical results suggest that centralized trading activities may enhance staking participation, and promote decentralization of the staking distribution through market incentives -- this partially justifies \texttt{BitMine}'s buy-and-stake strategy for ETH. We also study the effects of transaction costs and token supply mechanisms on the equilibrium staking ratio and concentration profile. These results illustrate how market microstructure and centralized liquidity provision can exert significant influence on decentralized blockchain protocols.

Optimization and Control.title: Global Extendability of Flat Cliques in Sparse Moment Relaxations
Optimization and Control.summary: Moment relaxations provide lower bounds for polynomial optimization problems, while the moment matrix carries more information than the bound itself. When the moment matrix satisfies the flat truncation condition, the bound is tight and global minimizers can be extracted from the matrix. In correlatively sparse relaxations, it is common that only some blocks are flat. We study whether such partial flatness still reveals part of a global minimizer. On a unicycle trajectory optimization problem, repeatedly extracting the atoms of flat cliques and fixing them recovers feasible, near-optimal trajectories. We then construct a counterexample whose relaxation is tight and has a rank-one flat clique, yet the unique extracted atom cannot be extended to a global minimizer. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for global extendability that involve only the boundary of a clique. Every extracted atom minimizes its clique objective given its boundary value, and when the bound is tight and the boundary moment block has rank at most one, the extracted atom of the clique is globally extendable.

Optimization and Control.title: Vanishing Events and Regularity-Conditioned Reachability in Linear Stieltjes Systems
Optimization and Control.summary: We study linear Stieltjes control systems in which actuation is concentrated at finitely many temporal events, and we ask what happens when one of those events progressively loses its atomic weight in the associated Stieltjes measure. For constant coefficients, ordinary finite-atomic reachability is governed by a truncated Krylov space and is therefore insensitive to the positive values of the event weights. A different picture emerges once trajectory regularity is imposed. In the supercritical super-$g$-Hölder regime, we minimize the largest event-normalized state jump and characterize exactly the terminal directions for which this cost remains uniformly bounded as a prescribed event weight tends to zero. The characterization combines what can be reached before the vulnerable event, a drift-cancellability condition at that event, and the directions that remain available afterwards. Ordinary reachability of the deleted-event system can therefore be strictly larger than bounded-cost reachability in the singular limit. We also separate two mechanisms of divergence: loss of ordinary reachability after deletion and failure of the intermediate compatibility condition. For compatible targets, the minimum cost converges to a constrained deleted-event problem. A dimensionless position--velocity benchmark motivated by pulsed proximity maneuvers shows the distinction explicitly.

Optimization and Control.title: Risk Control of Traffic Flow Through Chance Constraints and Large Deviation Approximation
Optimization and Control.summary: We develop a rare chance-constrained optimal control framework for autonomous traffic management, with traffic dynamics governed by stochastic partial differential equations. To efficiently enforce these probabilistic safety specifications, we exploit a large deviation theory (LDT) based approximation method, which converts the original highly non-convex, sampling-heavy stochastic optimization problem into a tractable deterministic nonlinear programming problem. The proposed LDT-based reformulation exhibits superior computational scalability, as its computational cost remains approximately constant regardless of the target violation probability, as opposed to the scaling challenge of traditional sampling-based methods. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is illustrated through numerical experiments on a ring road with stochastic on-ramp inflow, and evaluated with two representative risk measures, namely, maximum traffic density and speed variation. The results show that the proposed method keeps the violation probability close to the target without parameter tuning and is more than ten times faster than a risk-averse baseline.

Optimization and Control.title: Large player classes and approximately weighted voting
Optimization and Control.summary: It is known that completeness of the coalitional ($C$-)desirability relation in a simple game does not imply the existence of a weighted-majority representation. We show that weightedness is implied in an approximate sense. Call an $n$-player simple game $\varepsilon$-weighted if, for some weight vector in the $(n-1)$-simplex, any losing coalition weight exceeds any winning coalition weight by at most $\varepsilon$; let $\varepsilon^{\ast}$ be the smallest such $\varepsilon$. We establish an upper bound on $\varepsilon^{\ast}$ in a general $C$-complete game, and deduce that, if all classes of equally desirable players become large asymptotically but the number of classes is bounded, then $\varepsilon^{\ast}=O(1/n_{\min})$ for the minimal player class size $n_{\min}$, and the bound is tight. Importantly, the minimal attainable fraction $δ$ of coalitions mislabeled by a weighting rule also tends to $0$ when $n_{\min}\rightarrow\infty$ and the number of player classes is bounded, with $δ=O(1/\sqrt{n_{\min}})$.

Optimization and Control.title: Higher-Order Approximation of Exit Functionals in Sampling-Based Stochastic Model Predictive Control
Optimization and Control.summary: Safety evaluation in sampling-based stochastic model predictive control often requires numerical estimation of exit functionals. The approximation of first-exit times and exit indicators is therefore a key numerical bottleneck, and discretization error in these quantities directly affects the resulting controller. This paper studies how existing higher-order methods for strong approximation of exit times can be brought into safe control. Two cases are highlighted. For general noncommutative dynamics, an adaptive order-1 Milstein discretization is used together with Lévy-area simulation via Wiktorsson's method. For commutative dynamics, an adaptive order-1.5 construction achieves a stronger exit-time rate. Under a local anti-concentration condition on the exit-time law, we show that strong exit-time approximation transfers to strong approximation of the failure indicator. The methods are then studied in the context of chance-constrained path integral control, which provides an exact continuous-time representation of safety through exit events. Numerical experiments compare the two cases in terms of strong exit-time error, failure-indicator error, and closed-loop constraint satisfaction, showing improvement over Euler-Maruyama and thereby enabling existing and future techniques whose applicability depends on improved strong approximation.
Optimization and Control.comment: Accepted for publication in the proceedings of the 2026 IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC 2026). Minor correction to Assumption A4 and a typo fix relative to the conference version. Results are unchanged

Optimization and Control.title: Mitigating Performance Variability in Mixed-Integer Programming Solvers via LP State Steering
Optimization and Control.summary: Modern mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers repeatedly solve linear programming (LP) relaxations, but the LP state transferred from the simplex algorithm to the branch-and-bound tree is typically treated as an artifact of perturbation, presolve history, and numerical trajectory. This is harmless in pure linear programming, where alternative optimal bases certify the same bound. In MIP, however, those bases can expose distinct fractional structures, active rows, reduced costs, branching candidates, and reoptimization states. The inherited LP state is therefore an initial condition for the integer search. We exploit this initial condition to mitigate computational performance variability. The proposed framework generates alternative LP states on or near degenerate optimal faces, evaluates them within an auxiliary solver environment, and either selects a single state or executes a portfolio of candidate states in parallel. A handcrafted synthetic instance isolates the relationship between the initial LP state, the fractional profile, the branching trajectory, and the resulting node-count distribution: root-state steering reduces the weighted variability score~(WVS) by 67% over 1,000 paired seeds and produces no node-count regressions relative to default SCIP. On a separate 130-instance MIPLIB 2017 validation set with up to 50 paired seeds per instance, the top-five policy improves solve completion from 3,792 to 3,894 runs, reduces the shifted geometric mean of the recorded node count from 2,574.7 to 1,198.0, and lowers the median WVS by 9% on instances reliably solved by the baseline. These results demonstrate that the branch-and-bound phase inherits a specific LP state rather than merely an LP bound, and that the active management of this state systematically mitigates computational performance variability.

Optimization and Control.title: Failure Modes of Interior-Point SDP Solvers on Moment--SOS Hierarchies
Optimization and Control.summary: Standard semidefinite programming (SDP) solvers working in double precision can become unreliable on difficult problems, even when their output appears plausible. We study this issue for SDP problems arising from high-order moment-SOS hierarchies. Three polynomial optimization problems are analysed by comparing standard double-precision computations with reference solutions obtained using the extended-precision solver \mbox{Loraine\,64x4}. We observe two distinct patterns of numerical failure. In \emph{false convergence}, the computed bounds form a smooth sequence but approach the limit at the wrong rate. In \emph{stagnation}, the sequence develops a plateau or oscillations and no longer reflects the convergence of the underlying hierarchy. We introduce an empirical effective condition number based on the positive spectral components of the primal and dual solution matrices. It serves as a warning indicator rather than an error bound, and its growth accompanies numerical deterioration in our examples. We also examine the imbalance between primal and dual spectral conditioning and a Cholesky inverse residuum as potential diagnostic indicators. The results show that solver termination messages and apparently regular convergence curves may be insufficient to establish the reliability of high-order moment-SOS bounds.

Optimization and Control.title: Convergence of Sharpness-Aware Minimization Algorithms using Increasing Batch Size and Decaying Learning Rate
Optimization and Control.summary: The sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) algorithm and its variants, including gap guided SAM (GSAM), have been successful at improving the generalization capability of deep neural network models by finding flat local minima of the empirical loss in training. Meanwhile, it has been shown theoretically and practically that increasing the batch size or decaying the learning rate avoids sharp local minima of the empirical loss. In this paper, we consider the GSAM algorithm with increasing batch sizes or decaying learning rates, such as cosine annealing or linear learning rate, and theoretically show its convergence. Moreover, we numerically compare SAM (GSAM) with and without an increasing batch size and conclude that using an increasing batch size { achieves a lower worst-case $\ell_\infty$ adaptive sharpness} than compared with using a constant batch size and learning rate.

Optimization and Control.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Frank--Wolfe for Nonlinear Variational Inequalities on Polytopes
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider the Frank--Wolfe algorithm for solving variational inequalities over compact polytopes under a monotone $C^1$ operator $Φ$. The linear minimization oracle returns vertices, and we assume a coercivity condition on the Jacobian of $Φ$ at a solution. We prove last-iterate convergence to the unique solution at rate $O(k^{-\min\{α,1\}})$ for step sizes $γ_k=α/(k+β)$ with $β\geqα>0$. The bound holds uniformly over starting points and vertex tie-breaking. In particular, both $1/(k+1)$ and $2/(k+2)$ give $O(k^{-1})$ distance. A matching lower bound shows that this distance guarantee is worst-case order-optimal among prescribed admissible step-size schedules. We also obtain rates $O(k^{-\min\{α,1\}})$ for the Frank--Wolfe gap and $O(k^{-\min\{α,2\}})$ for the dual gap. These yield $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ and $O(\varepsilon^{-1/2})$ calls to each oracle for sustained gap accuracy $\varepsilon$ when $α\geq1$ and $α\geq2$, respectively, with instance-dependent constants. We also treat more general prescribed step-size schedules.

Optimization and Control.title: A Composite Representation Theorem for Solution Mappings in Regularized Composite Optimization with Applications to Hausdorff Lipschitz Stability
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the geometry and stability of solution mappings in regularized composite optimization, allowing multiple minimizers. We establish a composite representation that separates optimal linear images from their corresponding primal solutions through an image mapping and a generalized basis pursuit mapping. Under a fiber-attainment condition, the image mapping admits a reduced optimization formulation; neither representation requires convexity. For convex regularizers, suitable qualification conditions yield a Fenchel-conjugate representation of the reduced value function and a geometric characterization of the generalized basis pursuit mapping through affine fibers and a fixed lifting set. Using these representations, we establish sufficient conditions for local Hausdorff Lipschitz continuity of possibly set-valued solution mappings. We further show that the primal-space sufficient conditions imply the corresponding image-space conditions, with an additional injectivity requirement arising in the former. The results cover $\ell_1$-type and structured piecewise linear-quadratic regularizers under suitable assumptions. For classical $\ell_1$ regularization, our approach recovers an existing stability result without a finite sign-pattern decomposition. Numerical examples illustrate the recovery of complete solution sets, including a case with a nonpolyhedral graph of the generalized basis pursuit mapping.

Optimization and Control.title: A Feasible Direction Method with Active-Set Identification for Derivative-Free Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose a model-based trust region method for derivative-free optimization with simulation-based inequality constraints. We are motivated by settings of simulation optimization in which both function evaluations at infeasible points may be unreliable and constraint evaluations are expensive. Our method maintains feasible incumbents and computes steps from a subproblem suitable for a feasible-direction method in order to encourage generation of feasible trial points. To reduce the computational cost of modeling the constraints, we describe an active-set estimation scheme that permits modeling with only a subset of constraints in each subproblem, as opposed to maintaining models of all constraints. We show that every limit point of the incumbents generated by our method is a Fritz-John point, and is additionally a KKT point under the Mangasarian-Fromovitz constraint qualification. Under standard nondegeneracy conditions, the active-set estimate identifies, within finite time, all constraints active at the limit point of the incumbents. Experiments on CUTEst problems show that our method generates feasible trial points far more often than a comparable SQP-based approach and solves more problems within a given budget with fewer function evaluations.

Optimization and Control.title: Matching Randomized First-Order Bounds for Higher-Order Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: Does randomization improve the worst-case first-order complexity of nonconvex optimization when the objective is very smooth? We prove that, for every fixed finite integer $p\ge3$, finding an $\eps$-stationary point requires $Ω_p(\eps^{-5/3})$ exact value-and-gradient queries, even for $C^\infty$ objectives with initial gap at most one and simultaneous global Lipschitz budgets of one for derivatives of orders $1,\ldots,p$. Together with the known deterministic upper bound, this determines the accuracy exponent up to a single logarithmic factor. The lower bound holds for unrestricted adaptive randomized algorithms, unbounded query locations, and outputs that need not have been queried. One algorithm-independent hard distribution suffices in dimension $O_p(\eps^{-47/3})$. The construction combines a block-chain potential with an exact quartic core, repeated quadratic spectra, and two static Gaussian tensor perturbations. A scheduled Haar argument controls the entire adaptive query span. An innovation-only Gaussian comparison then bounds exact transcript information without assuming finite precision or a minimum query separation. This establishes the $5/3$ randomized accuracy barrier under every prescribed finite smoothness order, extending the previously matched third-order case.

Optimization and Control.title: Edge-preserving Bayesian neural networks via hierarchical sparsity-promoting priors
Optimization and Control.summary: Recovering piecewise-smooth functions with jump discontinuities from noisy, indirect, and incomplete data is a central task in computational inverse problems. Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) with heavy-tailed weight priors have emerged as effective edge-preserving priors for such problems. However, posterior inference for these models remains computationally challenging, and existing approaches settle for point estimates obtained by directly optimizing heavy-tailed log-densities. We propose GSBL-BNNs, which model the neural network parameters hierarchically using sparsity-promoting priors from generalized sparse Bayesian learning (GSBL). The hierarchical formulation recovers several popular marginal priors, including Laplace and Student's $t$ (including Cauchy). A key modeling ingredient, novel among edge-preserving BNNs and native to the hierarchical formulation, couples each neuron's bias to its weights through a shared hyperparameter, so that the induced jump discontinuities are free to occur anywhere in the domain while the conditionally Gaussian structure underlying efficient inference is preserved. Furthermore, we develop a block-coordinate descent (BCD) algorithm for maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation. This BCD approach alternates between standard network training with iteratively reweighted $\ell^2$-regularization and exact, closed-form hyperparameter updates for gamma and inverse gamma hyperpriors. Building on the BCD algorithm, we perform approximate Bayesian inference and uncertainty quantification (UQ) using deep ensembles. Computational experiments---including signal denoising, deblurring, and inverting a two-dimensional hyperbolic conservation law--- show that GSBL-BNNs deliver accurate, edge-preserving reconstructions with built-in UQ. Compared with Gaussian- and Cauchy-BNNs, they yield more accurate predictive means and avoid overconfident uncertainty estimates.

Optimization and Control.title: Matching Randomized Bounds for Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Concave Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We characterize the randomized component-oracle complexity of finite-sum nonconvex-concave optimization with a bounded dual domain. For $Φ(x)=\max_{y\in Y}n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x,y)$, the goal is to find an $\varepsilon$-stationary point of the Moreau envelope $Φ_{1/(2L)}$ with probability at least $2/3$ and a fixed query budget. Let $A=LΔ/\varepsilon^2$, $B=LD_Y/\varepsilon$, and $\bar B=\max\{1,B\}$, where $Δ$ bounds the initial primal gap and $D_Y$ bounds the dual diameter. For $A$ above a universal constant, the worst-case complexity is \[ \widetildeΘ\!\left(n+A\min\left\{ \sqrt n\,\bar B+\bar B^4,\ n^{3/4}\bar B\right\}\right). \] The bounds agree within constants for $B\le n^{1/4}$ and within one logarithm for larger $B$. Upper bounds require only mean-squared averaged smoothness and concavity of the average in the dual variable; lower bounds already hold under individual smoothness. The lower constructions cover adaptive component selection, arbitrary query norms, private randomization, and outputs that were never queried. A cone construction gives the small-diameter bound, while a serial branch construction and balanced replication give the remaining two regimes. On the upper side, a persistent estimator with primal averaging complements accelerated proximal dual steps equipped with an explicit primal certificate. The characterization takes the worst case over admissible known dual domains and finite dimensions.

Optimization and Control.title: On IDA-PBC with Maximum Energy Shapeability
Optimization and Control.summary: Interconnection and Damping Assignment Passivity-Based Control (IDA-PBC) is a well-established stabilization technique for affine nonlinear systems. However, its application is generally hindered by the requirement of solving a set of partial differential equations (PDEs), i.e., the so-called matching equation. This paper explores the notion of maximum energy shapeability which describes the scenario that the homogeneous part of the matching equation admits $m$ independent solutions with $m$ the dimension of the control input. We show that the maximum energy shapeability enables a systematic procedure for the IDA-PBC design by transforming the matching equation into a set of new PDEs. Specifically, the transformed matching equation admits an explicit solution in the single input case. Sufficient conditions for maximum energy shapeability are also provided. It is shown that some existing constructive IDA-PBC designs actually implicitly exploit the maximum energy shapeability. The proposed procedure for the IDA-PBC design is demonstrated with two practical examples.

Optimization and Control.title: Decision-Making in Digital Twins: Optimization, Control, and Learning
Optimization and Control.summary: A digital twin is a virtual representation of a physical system, continuously updated with data from the physical system, enabling dynamic information exchange and decision-making. This bidirectional interaction, which distinguishes digital twins from conventional simulation models, introduces new challenges to simulation-based optimization, control, and learning. This paper reviews recent developments in decision-making methodologies motivated by digital twins. We focus on three interconnected areas: simulation optimization, sequential decision making, and risk-aware decision making. For simulation optimization, we discuss data-driven simulation optimization under input uncertainty, streaming input data, decision-dependent observations, and limited computational and data-collection resources. For sequential decision making, we review the connections among digital twins, stochastic optimal control, and reinforcement learning, with emphasis on Bayesian approaches that update models and policies as new information becomes available. For risk-aware decision making, we discuss distributionally robust and Bayesian risk formulations as alternative approaches for addressing model uncertainty. Throughout the paper, we emphasize the common problem of making decisions while the underlying model is being updated. We conclude by identifying research challenges and opportunities.

Optimization and Control.title: Solution Set Dimensions in Convex Optimization and Primal-Polar Facial Signatures
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the possible dimensions of solution sets in linearly perturbed convex optimization problems and their behavior under convex duality. The dimensions of solution sets and inverse solution sets capture two complementary forms of nonuniqueness: that of optimal solutions for a given perturbation, and that of perturbations for which a given point is optimal. Although these two families are linked by Fenchel conjugacy, we show that their collections of dimensions can be prescribed independently for finite supercoercive convex functions. As a geometric consequence, we prove that the facial dimension signatures of a convex body and its polar can be prescribed independently. The connection between these two realization results is obtained by homogenizing the epigraphs of a function and its conjugate. In contrast, under simultaneous facial exposedness, we establish a dimensional obstruction relating the smallest positive proper face dimensions of the body and its polar. These results resolve two open questions posed by Roshchina and Tunçel.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal Recursive Composition and Dyadic Phase Laws for Gradient Descent with Predetermined Stepsizes
Optimization and Control.summary: Predetermined stepsize schedules featuring carefully chosen long steps have recently been shown to accelerate gradient descent (GD) on smooth convex functions. A prominent class of such schedules is built through recursive composition. In this paper, we characterize the convergence of these optimized recursive schedules, revealing a nonconstant log-periodic modulation across prescribed horizons. Specifically, we prove that for every $N \geq 1$, the optimized ConPP/OBS-S schedules satisfy $$f(x_{N-1})-f_\ast \le \frac{1}{2N^pΦ(\log_2N)-1} \frac{L}{2}\|x_0-x_\ast\|^2, \qquad p=\log_2(1+\sqrt2), $$ where $Φ$ is a positive, Lipschitz, nonconstant $1$-periodic function. We derive this by proving that balanced splitting is optimal at every horizon for these constructions, resolving a conjecture of Zhang and Jiang. Furthermore, for their asymmetric counterparts (ConPD/OBS-F schedules), we show that although optimal splits are not necessarily balanced, the same Silver exponent asymptotically persists alongside a distinct log-periodic modulation.

Optimization and Control.title: Extragradient and Past Extragradient Methods for $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz Variational Inequalities
Optimization and Control.summary: Variational inequalities (VIs) capture a broad class of optimization problems central to modern machine learning, including min-max optimization and equilibrium computation in multiplayer games. Traditionally, algorithms for solving VIs, such as Extragradient (EG) and Past Extragradient (PEG), have been analyzed under the standard $L$-Lipschitz assumption. However, this condition is often overly restrictive, and recent works have instead turned to the more relaxed $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz setting.
