A separate exploratory flight demonstrated two additional recoveries at 6.02 and 6.05 m/s within the same flight, exceeding the previously reported velocity for autonomous wall-collision recovery by 64%.
Robotics.comment: J.H. and L.G. contributed equally;S.L. and S.M. jointly advised;Supplementary video: https://youtu.be/Q76GmW9cNgE;Supported by EU Horizon Europe project SPEAR (grant no. 101119774);Submitted to ICRA 2027

Robotics.title: P-BFM: Perceptive Behavioral Foundation Models for Humanoid Control via Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning
Robotics.summary: Behavioral foundation models (BFMs) provide humanoids with reusable repertoires of whole-body behaviors; in real-world humanoid control, the same behavioral intent may require fundamentally different motions under different terrain constraints. Covering such variation with terrain-matched demonstrations requires enumerating a combinatorial space of behaviors and terrain geometries. We introduce P-BFM, a perceptive behavioral foundation model that factorizes humanoid control into terrain-invariant intent and terrain-conditioned realization. A forward-backward representation maps motion references, target states, and reward functions into a shared intent space without terrain information, while a perceptive policy learns how to realize each intent under the surrounding terrain geometry. We further identify a complementary limitation of purely latent control: behavioral latents can preserve local motion patterns while losing precise global progress. We therefore introduce Explicit Root Instructions (ERI), which separates global transport (e.g., heading and planar velocity) from behavioral intent, while leaving local whole-body adaptation to the perceptive policy. This decomposition leads to a characteristic capability absent from conventional BFMs: one fixed intent induces different, terrain-appropriate behaviors, including changes in step height, stride, posture, foothold placement, and contacts, without terrain-specific demonstrations. Across challenging terrains, P-BFM improves motion fidelity, root-control precision, and perturbation recovery over strong baselines. A single frozen policy further supports motion tracking, goal reaching, reward inference, teleoperation, and terrain-aware recovery, and transfers zero-shot to a Unitree G1 using onboard depth sensing.

Robotics.title: ReTrace: Cross-Stage Failure Attribution for Self-Improving Robotic Manipulation
Robotics.summary: General-purpose multimodal foundation models are increasingly capable of directly controlling robots, yet improving their manipulation capabilities through autonomous interaction remains challenging. A key challenge to such self-improvement is learning from failures in complex manipulation tasks involving cross-stage dependencies, where an action may succeed locally but cause a later stage to fail. To address this challenge, we introduce ReTrace, a self-improvement framework for robotic manipulation through autonomous physical interaction and retrospective reasoning, without provided demonstrations or model-parameter updates. ReTrace retrospectively traces downstream failures to earlier decisions, proposes targeted corrections, and evaluates them through subsequent interactions. Across attempts, ReTrace progressively consolidates validated corrections into a reusable manipulation skill that guide subsequent execution. We evaluate ReTrace on four real-world manipulation tasks using a Franka Research 3 robot. On the two tasks with strong cross-stage dependencies, GPT-6 Astra-low improves from 0% to 80% success on plug insertion and from 0% to 100% on ball pouring, while GPT-6 Sol-xhigh improves from 0% to 10% and 0% to 90%, respectively. The learned skills also transfer across model and reasoning configurations and reduce inference-time decision cost in most evaluated settings.

Robotics.title: Mission-Level Runtime Assurance for LLM-Assisted ISR Swarms over a Verification-Aware Fabric
Robotics.summary: Swarms of LLM-assisted autonomous robots are increasingly proposed for cooperative intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) in contested environments. A growing class of their assurance failures arises not within any single platform but across the swarm: individually-compliant actions compose into a mission-level violation: a prohibited objective split across platforms to evade per-platform limits, or a collective budget quietly exceeded. Per-platform guardrails miss these by construction, and contested communications let the violation hide behind lost or delayed evidence. We present a three-tier (platform/squad/mission) compositional runtime-verification framework that decomposes a mission policy into per-agent and cross-agent aspects, aggregates per-platform verdicts over a verification-aware messaging fabric, and fuses them with an evidence-aware, two-axis (security x completeness) algebra whose provenance names the platforms that jointly triggered a violation. Because the fabric makes evidence loss and silence observable, unsupported negative verdicts are downgraded to an explicit unknown rather than reported as mission-wide all-clears. On a simulated ISR mission, an indirect prompt injection that causes real LLM planners to split a prohibited collection task across four platforms is invisible to every per-platform monitor yet detected compositionally with full provenance; under an injected fault campaign a best-effort central monitor emits silent false all-clears while the verification-aware fabric emits none.

Robotics.title: $Δ$ Flow Matching for Robot Foundation Models
Robotics.summary: Flow matching is a common generative recipe for robot foundation models. Vision-language-action models (VLAs) generate action chunks, while world-action models (WAMs) additionally generate future visual states. Both start generation from a fixed Gaussian prior, despite temporal continuity between past and future states and actions. This requires costly training and iterative sampling, especially for WAMs with an additional visual branch. We introduce $Δ$-flow, which constructs the source from recent history with mild noise rather than from a fixed Gaussian prior. This moves the source closer to the target, reducing transport to a small residual $Δ$ that can be learned efficiently and enables single-step inference. We integrate $Δ$-flow into the VLA policy $π_{0.5}$ and the WAM policies ImageWAM and Fast-WAM. On LIBERO, ImageWAM reaches 90% success in one epoch rather than six, and Fast-WAM reaches 95% in two epochs rather than eight. With LoRA fine-tuning, $π_{0.5}$ exceeds its baseline's five-epoch performance after one epoch. Single-step inference gives $1.54\times$, $2.49\times$, and $4.45\times$ speedups on $π_{0.5}$, ImageWAM, and Fast-WAM, respectively. It preserves action smoothness, achieving a $4.5\times$ reduction in action jerk compared with one-step Gaussian sampling. $Δ$-flow reaches state-of-the-art generalization performance on LIBERO-Plus. Action-history sources can be applied to pretrained WAM policies without retraining. Replacing the Gaussian action source at inference largely preserves task success with a single sampling step and can slightly improve it. We further study how action representation and visual information in action learning affect history-to-future prediction in $Δ$-flow. These results show that $Δ$-flow is simple yet effective, improving the efficiency and generalization of robot foundation models.

Robotics.title: MedVLA: A Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Framework for Closed-Loop Precision Medical Robot Manipulation
Robotics.summary: Precision medical robotics demands adaptive decision-making under strict safety, interpretability, and execution constraints. Although recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models show strong multimodal reasoning ability, their continuous action generation paradigm is not well suited for precision medical tasks, where reliable closed-loop operation may also depend on non-action system function calls. To address this gap, we propose MedVLA, a hierarchical framework that couples high-level multimodal reasoning with low-level function-constrained execution. We further introduce a scalable multi-agent pipeline to generate skill-oriented chain-of-thought(CoT) data for structured training. Built on different multimodal large-model backbones, MedVLA consistently improves performance after fine-tuning, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework across model variants. Under identical initial conditions, we perform 100 closed-loop flexible electrode implantation trials. The results show that MedVLA achieves a 95.0\% task success rate, substantially outperforming representative VLA baselines, including OpenVLA (8\%) and $π_0$ (15\%), in accuracy, stability, and safety. These results indicate that structured reasoning with constrained function-level execution is a practical route toward deployable precision medical robotics.

Robotics.title: Hand2Robot: Object-Centric 4D Hand Reconstruction from Human Demonstrations for Robotics
Robotics.summary: Human demonstrations can capture task-relevant manipulation without using the target robot, but the recorded hand motions cannot directly serve as robot action supervision. Hand reconstruction and motion retargeting provide a direct route to such supervision, yet recovering hand motion alone does not ensure physically consistent hand-object interactions. To address this issue, we introduce Hand2Robot, an object-centric 4D hand reconstruction framework for robot policy post-training. Given videos of humans performing the target task, Hand2Robot extracts interaction clips, reconstructs object geometry, and generates robot action supervision through hand-object interaction optimization and motion retargeting. For object tracking, we combine observation confidence with temporal motion constraints to select a globally consistent object pose trajectory from per-frame pose candidates. For hand refinement, we use object geometry and motion as a reference and combine staged 2D alignment with object-local contact constraints to refine hand trajectories and finger joint configurations. Experiments on DexYCB and HO3D-v3 show improved object pose accuracy and hand-object interaction quality. Experiments on three real-robot dexterous manipulation tasks further show that reconstructed and retargeted human demonstrations can effectively supplement limited robot data for target-task policy post-training.
Robotics.comment: 21 pages, including appendix. Project page: https://hand2robot.github.io/

Optimization and Control.title: Nonlinear Feedback Control in High Dimensions using the Polynomial-Polynomial Regulator
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider the problem of computing Taylor approximations to the optimal feedback law and value function for infinite-horizon finite-dimensional nonlinear optimal control problem---also known as Al'brekht's method. The scalability of existing Al'brekht-based approaches to computing approximate solutions to the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation associated with the optimal control problem has been severely limited by computational resources. The computational time issue has been partially mitigated by recent works leveraging tensor-structure to develop efficient numerical methods. However, RAM requirements still have remained a major hindrance to scaling beyond state dimensions of a few hundred or low thousands. We propose an acceleration to compute the expensive higher-order terms in a reduced space, mitigating the curse of dimensionality. A fast and scalable \textsc{Matlab} implementation is provided open-source for general purpose use, with the ability to accommodate arbitrary polynomial nonlinearities in the control-affine state equation, as well as polynomial state-dependence in the cost function, and the ability to handle systems in generalized form with a non-identity mass matrix, such as finite element models. Combined with the exploitation of sparsity and modern low-rank Riccati solvers, this permits computing approximations to polynomial feedback laws based on Al'brekht's method in hundreds of thousands of states.

Optimization and Control.title: Comparing Socially-Equitable Renewable Energy Budget Allocation MDP Policies in Mature and Emerging Economies
Optimization and Control.summary: Equitable renewable-energy planning is a sequential decision problem, but the decision variables available to a public planner differ sharply between mature and emerging economies. In the former the government largely builds generation, while in the latter it steers private investment through incentives and quotas. We formulate socially-equitable renewable-energy budget allocation as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and, using a single problem-agnostic solver interface, compare the same policies across the two settings: eight U.S. cities (a mature economy) and West Java, Indonesia (an emerging economy). The results show that across both settings, a receding-horizon value-iteration policy dominates. In the U.S., it reaches 66% renewable penetration while cutting the underserved low-income population by 96% versus a random baseline. In West Java it closes the low-access gap while crowding in about seven times the private capital of a naive market-chasing heuristic. More interestingly, this heuristic, which is mildly sub-optimal in the U.S., could yield catastrophic outcomes in Indonesia, by underserving every low-access region, because chasing attractive markets and serving the underserved diverge once the planner acts through private developers.

Optimization and Control.title: An Efficient, Lean 4 Verified Necessary and Sufficient Condition for Membership in Pedigree Polytopes
Optimization and Control.summary: The set \(P_{n}\) consists of the characteristic vectors of pedigrees, which are combinatorial encodings in one-to-one correspondence with Hamiltonian cycles. For \(n \geq 4\) and \(τ_{n} = \binom{n}{3}-1\), the Membership Problem for the Pedigree Polytope (M3P) asks whether a given vector \(X \in \mathbb{Q}^{τ_{n}}\) belongs to \(\mathrm{conv}(P_n)\). This paper gives a complete account, with the full proof statements and machine-verified Lean~4 certificates, of the necessary and sufficient (\NS) condition established in Chapter~5 of \emph{Pedigree Polytopes: New Insights on Computational Complexity of Combinatorial Optimisation Problems} (Arthanari, 2023): membership of $X$ in $\mathrm{conv}(P_n)$ is characterised by the feasibility, at every stage $k=4,\dots,n-1$, of a recursively constructed layered network, together with, when needed, a multicommodity flow problem $\mathrm{MCF}(k-1)$ achieving its maximum possible flow $z_{\max}$. We present the construction, the \NS{} condition itself, and the proofs of this characterisation, together with the resulting polynomial-time algorithm for M3P. Both directions of the \NS{} condition --- sufficiency and necessity (the multicommodity-flow feasibility argument of the book's Chapter~5) --- are machine-verified in Lean~4/Mathlib4 with zero unresolved \texttt{sorry}s in either dependency chain. The \NS{} characterisation therefore follows directly from the two machine-checked implications. The complete Lean~4 project is publicly available. A companion introductory article (arXiv:2507.09069) presents the same material for a broader readership, without the Lean~4 verification; the present paper adds full statements, proof sketches, and the complete machine-checked certificates.

Optimization and Control.title: Two Linear Programs are Better than One
Optimization and Control.summary:
The extension complexity $\operatorname{xc}(P)$ of a polytope $P$ is the minimum number of facets of a polytope that projects onto it. Motivated by the complexity of neural networks, Hertrich and Loho introduced the virtual extension complexity $\operatorname{vxc}(P)$ of a polytope $P$, which is the minimum of $\operatorname{xc}(Q) + \operatorname{xc}(R)$ among all polytopes $Q$ and $R$ such that $P+Q=R$. We show the following results pertaining to virtual extension complexity.
  First, we resolve the core open problem on the topic by showing the virtual extension complexity can be exponentially smaller than extension complexity. Second, we show there are matroid base polytopes with exponential virtual extension complexity by adapting a semi-algebraic counting argument by Hrubeš that extends the counting arguments of Rothvoss. Finally, we show that the maximum virtual extension complexity of a polygon with $n$ vertices is $Θ(\sqrt{n})$. This resolves an analogue of a question on extension complexity of Fiorini, Rothvoss, and Tiwary in 2011 in the case of virtual extension complexity.

Optimization and Control.title: The $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance via $3\times3$ block matrices (with application to $p$-Bures-Wasserstein barycenters)
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance $D_p(A,B)=(\mathrm{tr}\,A^p+\mathrm{tr}\,B^p-2\|A^{1/2}B^{1/2}\|_p^p)^{1/2}$ on positive semidefinite matrices; it equals the Bures-Wasserstein distance for $p=1$, and the Hilbert-Schmidt distance for $p=2$. We prove that $D_p$ is a metric for every $1\le p\le2$, by proving a stronger 2014 conjecture of Lin and van den Driessche on $3\times3$ block matrices. Our main tool is a partition inequality for Schatten norms, proved by complex interpolation. We also characterize Fréchet means for $D_p$ by a fixed-point equation and prove geometric convergence of the associated iteration.

Optimization and Control.title: Tight Complexity of Muon under Heavy-Tailed Noise
Optimization and Control.summary: A growing lesson from neural network optimization is that optimizer design should respect how the model is parametrized. The layerwise input-output structure of neural networks motivates Muon and Scion, whose updates also support hyperparameter transfer. At the same time, stochastic gradient noise in deep learning is often far from sub-Gaussian and may exhibit heavy tails. These observations have shaped recent algorithmic principles for training neural networks, yet their joint theoretical consequences are underexplored. In particular, it is unclear what dimension dependence is unavoidable for gradient-based methods when the problem class is defined using an input-output norm and the stochastic gradient noise is heavy-tailed, and if higher-order smoothness can accelerate optimization. We study these questions through nonconvex smooth stochastic optimization over $\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ equipped with general norms and under $p^\mathrm{th}$-moment heavy-tailed noise, where the goal is to achieve an $ε$-stationary point in the dual norm. Our first contribution is a dimension-dependent lower bound: when $\max\{m,n\}$ is large enough, any method using only the stochastic gradients requires $Ω(\min\{m, n\}ε^{-\frac{3p-2}{p-1}})$ oracle calls for the problem class defined by the spectral norm, which is a common input-output matrix norm. We prove that a batched Muon method with the spectral norm can achieve the matching upper bound of $O(\min\{m, n\}ε^{-\frac{3p-2}{p-1}})$. To exploit higher-order smoothness, we propose a transported Muon method and improve the bound to $O(\min\{m, n\}ε^{-\frac{5p-3}{2p-2}})$ when the norm is spectral and the Hessian is Lipschitz. Finally, we incorporate practical heuristics into our transported method and evaluate it across multiple architectures and model sizes, showing its compatibility with neural network training.

Optimization and Control.title: Entropy-Regularized Mean-Field Games with Average-Reward Criterion: Span-Seminorm Contractions and Model-Free Learning
Optimization and Control.summary: We study stationary discrete-time mean-field games with finite state and action spaces under the average-reward criterion, with an entropy-regularized objective and population-dependent dynamics and rewards. Under a minorization condition, the soft Q-operator is a span-seminorm contraction for the full transition kernel, so relative value iteration does not require the minorizing measure. When the Lipschitz constant of the kernel is below the minorization mass and the temperature exceeds an explicit threshold, the equilibrium fixed-point operator is a contraction: an equilibrium exists, its population distribution is unique, and a fixed-point iteration converges to it geometrically. We then learn the equilibrium model-free from a simulator, combining soft Q-learning at a fixed population distribution with an empirical transition kernel. We prove a finite-sample bound for soft Q-learning in the span seminorm, with temperature-independent constants, and derive convergence rates for the learned population distribution and policy. A congestion-aware routing game illustrates the results.

Optimization and Control.title: On the Convergence of Constrained Gradient Method
Optimization and Control.summary: The constrained gradient method (CGM) has recently been proposed to solve convex optimization and monotone variational inequality (VI) problems with general functional constraints. While existing literature has established convergence results for CGM, the assumptions employed therein are quite restrictive; in some cases, certain assumptions are mutually inconsistent, leading to gaps in the underlying analysis. This paper derives rigorous and improved convergence guarantees for CGM under weaker and more reasonable assumptions, covering strongly convex optimization problems, as well as VI problems under both strongly monotone and general monotone settings. Preliminary numerical experiments are provided to verify the validity of CGM and demonstrate its efficacy in addressing such problems.

Optimization and Control.title: Cosm: orchestrated collective dynamics give rise to rapid computational search at the solution frontier
Optimization and Control.summary: We introduce Collective Switched Motion (Cosm), a heuristic optimization framework based on orchestrated collective dynamics. Cosm organizes the objective into conflict-minimized subobjectives and activates them sequentially, temporally separating competing local influences. The interplay of switching and local interactions among variables, supplemented by structured correlated perturbations, gives rise to collective search behavior including coordinated cluster motion. Using this framework, we develop and test a solver for sparse Ising optimization. On G64, a large sparse instance with a highly heterogeneous degree distribution from the longstanding Gset Max-Cut benchmark suite, Cosm establishes a new best-known cut of 8753. On large random-graph instances G61 and G70, whose best-known cuts of 5799 and 9595 have been difficult for prior heuristics to attain, a vectorized CPU implementation of Cosm reliably reaches these cuts with times-to-target of 15 s and 2.4 s, respectively. Cosm also heuristically attains the certified optimum of G81, the largest Gset instance (a 20,000-variable two-dimensional spin glass), along with those of G72 and G77. Tests on planted-solution spin-glass benchmarks suggest more favorable empirical scaling than that previously reported for seven compared solvers. Cosm demonstrates that, from simple interacting elements and a new form of orchestration, effective search can emerge.

Optimization and Control.title: Quantum ordinal optimization under a fixed comparison budget
Optimization and Control.summary: Ordinal optimization selects designs that are good enough rather than optimal when evaluation is expensive and the budget is small. The alignment probability measures the chance that the selected set contains at least a prescribed number of truly good designs. We formulate quantum ordinal optimization as a class of problems that maximize this probability under a fixed oracle budget. We study exact, coherent pairwise comparisons with one selected design as a first instance, with the budget counted in comparison queries. For every classical comparison budget smaller than the number of designs, we prove that a knockout among uniformly sampled designs attains the optimum. The sample is drawn without replacement and contains one more design than the number of comparisons. For a uniformly random order, the selected design's rank has a polynomial probability law. At the same comparison budget, the maximum quantum degree is at most twice the classical maximum, a factor attained whenever there are more than twice as many designs as comparisons, so a quantum algorithm can realize rank laws that no classical algorithm with the same budget can. We determine the exact quantum optimum with one comparison for every number of designs and every good-enough set. For selecting the best of n designs, the optimal success probability with one quantum comparison is approximately 3.30/n for large n, compared with 2/n for one classical comparison. When the best design is sought, one quantum comparison gives a higher alignment probability than two classical comparisons whenever there are more than nine designs.

Optimization and Control.title: Learning linear dynamical systems under convex constraints
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider the problem of finite-time identification of linear dynamical systems from $T$ samples of a single trajectory. Recent results have predominantly focused on the setup where either no structural assumption is made on the system matrix $A^* \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$, or specific structural assumptions (e.g. sparsity) are made on $A^*$. We assume prior structural information on $A^*$ is available, which can be captured in the form of a convex set $\mathcal{K}$ containing $A^*$. For the solution of the ensuing constrained least squares estimator, we derive non-asymptotic error bounds in the Frobenius norm that depend on the local size of $\mathcal{K}$ at $A^*$. To illustrate the usefulness of these results, we instantiate them for four examples, namely when (i) $A^*$ is sparse and $\mathcal{K}$ is a suitably scaled $\ell_1$ ball; (ii) $\mathcal{K}$ is a subspace; (iii) $\mathcal{K}$ consists of matrices each of which is formed by sampling a bivariate convex function on a uniform $n \times n$ grid (convex regression); (iv) $\mathcal{K}$ consists of matrices each row of which is formed by uniform sampling (with step size $1/T$) of a univariate Lipschitz function. In all these situations, we show that $A^*$ can be reliably estimated for values of $T$ much smaller than what is needed for the unconstrained setting.

Optimization and Control.title: Controllability of finite-dimensional linear fractional systems under uncertain parameters
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper investigates the controllability of finite-dimensional linear fractional systems involving an uncertain parameter. We establish new results on the simultaneous and average controllability. In particular, we show that average controllability can be characterized by the so-called average Kalman rank condition and the average Gramian matrix. Moreover, using the average Gramian matrix, we design an open-loop control with minimal energy. These results can be seen as a natural generalization of the classical results known for systems with integer-order derivatives. Finally, numerical simulations are provided to robustly validate the theoretical findings, with a focus on the fractional Rössler system for a damping parameter following either a Gaussian or a uniform distribution.

Optimization and Control.title: Fast Trainable Multilinear Bases for Image Compression
Optimization and Control.summary: The Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT), the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT), and their block-wise variants underpin most deployed image and video codecs. Their effectiveness rests on three properties: their runtime is near-linear (up to a polylogarithmic factor) in the image size, they are exactly invertible, and they carry few to no parameters. We generalize these transforms to dataset-adaptive isometric multilinear bases that keep all three properties at the cost of a polylogarithmic number of parameters, by parameterizing each basis as an isometric tensor network, inspired by quantum many-body theory, and training one shared basis per image dataset with Riemannian optimization. Because the family contains the DFT and the DCT-IV (a variant of the DCT) as exact points, training can start from these transforms, and it improves on its starting point at the compression level it is trained for. We evaluate the bases on natural photographs and line drawings. On photographs, which the cosine basis already fits well, the best trained basis leads the DCT only under aggressive truncation. On Quick Draw line drawings, under a common codec at matched quality, the best trained basis stores each image in about 20% fewer bytes than the 8x8 block cosine transform of the Joint Photographic Experts Group (JPEG) format, not counting the one-off storage of the basis.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal and Self Selection of Service Type in a Queueing System where Long Service Postpones the Need for the Next Service
Optimization and Control.summary: We study a make-to-order system with a finite set of customers. Production is stochastic with a nonlinear dependence between the ordered quantity and the production rate. Customers may have to queue until their turn arrives, and therefore their order decisions interact. Specifically, while being served, customers are aware of the queue length and choose one of two order quantities (or service types). The time to the next replenishment (their activity time) is stochastic and depends on the order quantities. A customer is inactive during service and while waiting in the queue. We refer to the type of service with a greater ratio of expected activity to service time as ``more efficient''. In the centralized case, the system is interested in maximizing the steady-state average number of active customers, which is referred to as the efficiency of the system. We show that choosing the more efficient service is not always optimal, but the optimal strategy can be approximated well by selecting one of three threshold strategies which depend on the number of inactive customers. In the decentralized case, each customer acts to maximize the fraction of time she is active. We observe that individuals and the manager have opposite incentives: When the queue is long, individuals tend to choose the long service, while the manager prefers the short service in this case. This makes the system difficult to regulate. However, we show that simply removing the less efficient service significantly increases efficiency.

Optimization and Control.title: Homogenization of an optimal control problem for a Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system in a 3D perforated domain
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the homogenization of an optimal control problem governed by a Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system in a periodically perforated three-dimensional domain. The obstacles are Lipschitz sets of size $\varepsilon^α$, $α>3$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period. The fluid satisfies the no-slip condition on the outer boundary and the free-slip condition on the obstacles, the phase-field equation contains a source term, and the convective term carries a pore-scale Reynolds number that tends to zero as $\varepsilon\to0$. The control is a distributed body force, and the cost functional tracks the velocity in $L^2$ and the order parameter in $H^1$. Since uniqueness of weak solutions of the state system is not known for fixed $\varepsilon$, the control-to-state relation is multivalued, and we pose the microscopic problems over control-state pairs. We prove the existence of microscopic optimal pairs and the sequential $Γ$-convergence of the cost functionals to the cost functional of a control problem governed by the unsteady Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system on the full domain. As a consequence, the optimal values converge, every cluster point of microscopic optimal pairs is optimal for the homogenized problem, and the optimal controls converge strongly along the corresponding subsequences. The $\liminf$ inequality follows from the homogenization of the state system, including the strong convergence of the gradients of the order parameter. Only the recovery sequence requires uniqueness of weak solutions of the homogenized system, which we prove when the outer boundary is of class $C^{2,1}$.

Optimization and Control.title: Eigenvalue-Decomposition Cost Denoising for Predict-then-Optimize
Optimization and Control.summary: Predict-then-optimize methods learn a mapping from features to unknown edge costs. They then solve the shortest-path problem on the predicted costs. We study a feature-free alternative for the case where the decision-maker observes many noisy cost vectors on a fixed network. The cost vectors are denoised by an eigenvalue decomposition (PCA) of their covariance matrix. Dijkstra's algorithm then runs on the result. We test this on the $5\times5$ grid of \citet{elmachtoub2022}, with $1000$ independent replications and a fresh ground truth in each. We compare against SPO+, against naive Dijkstra on noisy costs, and against two alternatives to a hand-picked rank $k$ (the Gavish-Donoho threshold and a Ledoit-Wolf filter). We also test a hybrid of SPO+ and PCA. Four findings emerge. First, the rank matters. Keeping $k=2$ components performs worse than no denoising. Second, when costs are close to linear in the features, the Gavish-Donoho threshold recovers the true rank without supervision. PCA-denoised Dijkstra outperforms SPO+ at $°=1$, but underperforms SPO+ at $°\geq 2$. The hybrid works best at $°=1$ and is slightly better than SPO+ at $°=2$. Third, when costs are strongly nonlinear ($°=4$), the signal is no longer low-rank, and only the Ledoit-Wolf filter clearly beats the naive baseline. Fourth, the benefit of denoising grows with network size on grids, but not on a layered non-grid network at high nonlinearity.

Optimization and Control.title: KKT Residual Sliding Manifolds: A Projection-Free Structured Finite-Time Solver for Nonlinear Constrained Optimisation
Optimization and Control.summary: Nonlinear Constrained Optimisation (NCO) requires simultaneous satisfaction of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions. Existing methods enforce these conditions through projections, penalties, barriers, or sequential approximations, potentially introducing computational complexity and convergence difficulties. For nonconvex problems, a KKT point need not be a local optimum. This paper reformulates NCO as stabilisation of a unified KKT sliding residual manifold and develops SM-KKT, a projection-free solver. Stationarity, equality feasibility, and regularised Fischer-Burmeister complementarity are integrated into a unified residual system, with complementarity encoding inequality feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness. The manifold's zero set is shown to be equivalent to the KKT conditions. The required Jacobian saddle-point inertia is characterised and shown, under stated assumptions, to be equivalent to the simultaneous satisfaction of the Linear Independence Constraint Qualification (LICQ) and Second-Order Sufficient Condition (SOSC). This characterisation establishes local stability of the structured correction algorithm under these conditions and distinguishes nondegenerate locally optimal KKT solutions from points failing second-order optimality. SM-KKT computes structured primal--dual corrections and applies a discrete sliding reaching law to drive the KKT residual into a prescribed boundary layer in finite time. Four nonlinear benchmarks show recovery of reference constrained optima with KKT residuals below $10^{-6}$, earlier boundary-layer reaching, and favourable KKT accuracy compared with projected primal-dual, augmented-Lagrangian, quadratic-penalty, and log-barrier baselines.

Optimization and Control.title: Beyond Aggregate Drift: Optimal Client-Specific Windows in Federated Learning
Optimization and Control.summary:
We study federated learning from continuously arriving data: each client samples from its own distribution, these distributions drift over time, and the server must track the minimizer of the clients' weighted average loss. Clients are not alike as they collect data at different rates, with different noise, and change at different speeds. The main question is how much history should each one keep? A single shared window must serve every client at once, and so makes a fast-changing client carry the sampling noise of a slow, nearly stationary one.
  We give each client a memory of its own, sized to that client's noise, arrival rate, and drift, and refresh it by restarted accelerated method that starts from a common point. The tracking error is then bounded by \[
  R\left(\sum_m w_m^{3/2}\,σ_m\sqrt{γ_m/λ_m}\right)^{2/3}, \] for clients with weight $w_m$, noise $σ_m$, arrival rate $λ_m$, and drift rate $γ_m$ on a domain of diameter $R$. This is never worse than what any common window can achieve, and strictly better whenever noise and drift are spread unevenly across clients.
  A lower bound that puts different groups of clients on different drift clocks shows this quantity is the right one. The two bounds agree up to a constant whenever the clients occupy boundedly many refresh scales, and in general differ only by the sixth root of the number of scales. Experiments show the gain comes from the memory rather than from the solver: it persists across accelerated, stochastic-gradient, and one-step methods, and against a separately tuned common-memory baseline.

Optimization and Control.title: From Product Evidence to Access Rights: Auditing and Routing Non-Firm Grid Connections
Optimization and Control.summary: Non-firm connection products can accelerate grid access while reinforcements are delayed, but their planning value depends on evidence supporting the contractual promise. We develop a one-way evidence-to-access framework for calendarized products. Stage A constructs and fixes directional restriction calendars from public residual-load and day-ahead price-timing signals. Stage B audits the submitted calendar and one bounded common repair, tests joint threshold attainability under the shared annual budget, and applies an aggregation-aware Power Transfer Distribution Factor (PTDF) certificate. Stage C treats the resulting ledger as fixed in queue-aware allocation and intervention planning. In the primary policy-package evaluation, the evidence-supported menu returns the same $2.119$~GW allocation as firm-only access, whereas authorizing the uniformly derated fallback raises awards to $6.442$~GW and reduces backlog from $136.076$ to $113.601$~GW-years; all $4.489$~GW of non-firm awards use the fallback. In a target-free matched control, evidence-routed and state-blind fallback menus attain primary objectives equivalent within EUR~1 and return the same accepted applicants, award years, routes, and intervention portfolio. Thus, in the reported testbed, fallback authorization rather than calendar-specific evidence support drives the access-volume effect.

Optimization and Control.title: Sparsity in control problems: Recent trends and open challenges
Optimization and Control.summary: As in all fields of engineering, control engineers constantly face a dichotomy between achieving high performance and the limited availability of resources for sensing, actuation, and control. This tension often translates into formalizing design problems with sparsity constraints; that is, the design involves decision variables whose number, spatial reach, temporal spread, or other physical expressions are much smaller than in the ideal scenario of unconstrained optimization of a task-related performance metric. Even though this fundamental limitation underlines a plethora of methodological approaches and application domains, the control literature is fragmented into several lines of work tailored to specific scenarios. This survey fills the gap by bringing together several lines of work on handling sparsity in relevant control problems such as actuator scheduling, minimal-energy controllability, maximum hands-off control, and online convex optimization, and weaving a red thread through theoretical foundations and algorithms. Beyond establishing a coherent, structured narrative of problems and solutions for handling sparsity in control scenarios, we discuss open areas and relevant directions for future research, motivated by the growing complexity of control systems and their relations with key domains such as pervasive computing, distributed learning, cyberphysical security, and ecological footprint.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal Cuts and Optimal Faces of Exact Max-Cut Semidefinite Relaxations
Optimization and Control.summary: An exact Max-Cut semidefinite relaxation can have optima outside the convex hull of optimal cut matrices. We study when this hull equals the optimal face and how to recognize equality. For rational weights, the unique optimal dual slack is recoverable in polynomial time, but its kernel may contain directions no optimal matrix uses. Under strict complementarity, recognition and recovery of all optimal cuts on equality instances take deterministic polynomial time. At dual rank one, this hypothesis is unnecessary. Recognition is polynomial-time Turing equivalent to exact rational semidefinite feasibility, even on simple unweighted graphs. Testing whether a supplied cut matrix is the unique optimum is many-one equivalent, even on connected simple graphs with a unique optimal cut. NP-completeness of recognition would imply NP equals coNP. Replication realizes doubly nonnegative matrices with positive diagonal and rational kernel as sign-spanned optimal dual slacks, preserving rank, complete positivity, and cp-rank.

Optimization and Control.title: Modified Polyhedral Method to Elicit Shape-Free Utility and Reduction of Conservatism in Robust Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we propose a modified polyhedral method to elicit a decision maker's (DM's) nonlinear univariate utility function without explicit knowledge of its shape, Lipschitz modulus, or inflection point. Inspired by \cite{THS04} for linear multivariate utility elicitation, we extend the polyhedral method to the nonlinear setting by addressing two major challenges. First, we approximate the nonlinear utility function using a continuous piecewise linear function (PLF) represented by its increment vector, such that utility elicitation can be viewed as progressively reducing a polyhedral feasible region of increment vectors. Second, we iteratively shrink this polyhedron through hyperplane cuts generated from pairwise lottery comparisons. Since PLF approximation errors may cause the resulting hyperplanes to deviate from ideal cutting directions, we dynamically enrich the PLF by incorporating newly generated lottery outcomes as additional breakpoints. The elicited responses are then used to construct an ambiguity set of utility functions for decision making under worst-case expected utility. To mitigate the potential conservatism of the resulting maximin model, we use the analytic center of the ambiguity set as a nominal estimate of the DM's utility increment vector and derive, through dual reformulation, a flexible weighting scheme for controlling conservatism. The resulting model accommodates asymmetric bounds on utility increments around the analytic center and admits a single mixed-integer linear programming reformulation for piecewise linear utilities. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed elicitation method and conservatism-reduction approach. Finally, we discuss several potential extensions, including applications to multivariate nonlinear utility elicitation and dynamic pricing problems.

Optimization and Control.title: Bilinear Mamba-Koopman Neural MPC for Varying Dynamics
Optimization and Control.summary:
Koopman-based neural MPC models generate time-varying dynamics from historical data, but preserve convexity by enforcing that the system operator is independent of the current control input. This conditional independence constraint limits adaptation to changing dynamics within a single MPC horizon, particularly under time-varying conditions and under stale-plan execution.
  We propose Bilinear Mamba-Koopman Neural MPC, a minimal extension that introduces control-dependent coupling in the latent dynamics, allowing the effective operator to adapt to the current input. The resulting model is a strict generalization of the standard linear, conditional-independence formulation, adds less than 1% parameters through a low-rank structure, and admits exact model Jacobians that enable efficient Sequential Convex Programming (SCP) with monotone-descent and KKT convergence results under standard trust-region assumptions.
  Across CartPole and RSCP benchmarks in time-invariant and time-varying regimes, the proposed model matches or improves forecasting accuracy on every cell when training noise is averaged out, with strict gains where control-state coupling is structurally present. Its main closed-loop gains appear in the RSCP TV task, where iterative SCP improves adaptation within the horizon and substantially stabilizes training; in CartPole TV, the gains are modest but consistent. In delayed re-planning experiments on the time-varying variants, the bilinear model degrades more gracefully under stale-plan execution, maintaining a consistent advantage on CartPole TV and a substantially larger robustness margin on RSCP TV. These results show that control-dependent latent dynamics provide a simple and effective mechanism for robust MPC under varying conditions.

Optimization and Control.title: Cyclic steepest descent is $R$-superlinearly convergent for almost every initialization on two-spectrum quadratics
Optimization and Control.summary:
We completely classify cyclic steepest descent (CSD) on strictly convex quadratics whose Hessian has exactly two distinct eigenvalues. At the beginning of each cycle CSD recomputes an exact steepest-descent stepsize and reuses it for $m$ updates. For every $m\ge2$, write $A=aP+bQ$ with $0<a<b$ and spectral projectors $P,Q$. For nonzero spectral blocks, let $r=\|Pg\|_2/\|Qg\|_2$ at a cycle boundary. The exact projective dynamics is $r^+=r^{1-2m}$. Hence the nonzero equal-norm cone $\|Pg_0\|_2=\|Qg_0\|_2>0$ is precisely the nonterminating exceptional set: there the convergence is $R$-linear with factor $(b-a)/(b+a)$, whereas every other nonterminating initialization is $R$-superlinear and one-eigenspace initializations terminate in one step. The exceptional cone has Lebesgue measure zero, so $R$-superlinear convergence holds almost everywhere in this two-spectrum class.
  The main results of this paper were obtained through a generative-AI workflow using OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, Anthropic Claude Fable 5, and OpenAI GPT-6 Astra. Further details appear in the disclosure at the end of the paper.

Optimization and Control.title: Explicit Bounds on Hoffman Constants for Sparse Polyhedral Regularizers
Optimization and Control.summary: Hoffman constants quantify the distance to the solution set of a polyhedral system in terms of its residual; they control error bounds, geometric conditioning, the convergence rate of first-order iterative algorithms, and the stability of regression estimators to target perturbations. Despite their importance, explicit values of Hoffman constants are rarely available due to their computational complexity. In this paper, we derive explicit bounds on the Hoffman constant for a class of structured polyhedral systems arising in sparse regularization. We show that the constants admit a decomposition into spectral, geometric, and interaction components, which together determine their scaling behavior. This framework explains the gap between worst-case dimension-dependent bounds and the favorable conditioning observed empirically in structured problems. As a primary application, we analyze $\ell_1$-regularized least squares, demonstrating that the effective constants depend on low-dimensional active subspaces rather than the ambient dimension. We then extend to the elastic net and adaptive $\ell_1$-regularized formulations, demonstrating how the underlying optimization geometry is altered by the $\ell_2$ penalty and reweighting scheme. Furthermore, we relate our results to classical statistical assumptions and show that the restricted eigenvalue condition bounds only the primal curvature of the active set, leaving the dual interaction geometry unconstrained and is thus insufficient alone for fast theoretical convergence rates. We further show standard $\ell_\infty$ coherence conditions do not yield dimension-independent Euclidean bounds to close this gap. Our theoretical results show that Hoffman constants admit explicit, interpretable forms in structured regression settings and, in practice, provide actionable tools for post-hoc feature pruning and a priori optimal hyperparameter selection.

Information Retrieval.title: The Impact of AI Search on the Online Content Ecosystem: Evidence from Google and Reddit
Information Retrieval.summary: Search engines traditionally complement online content platforms by directing users seeking information to external websites. The emergence of generative AI search tools that summarize answers directly on the results page may disrupt this relationship by making visits to source platforms optional. We study this question using Google AI Overviews and Reddit, one of the largest online discussion platforms. Our identification exploits Google's content moderation policy: Safe-for-Work (SFW) Reddit communities are indexed by Google organic search and surfaced in Google AI Overviews, while Not-Safe-for-Work (NSFW) communities, though indexed by organic search, are prohibited from being referenced in AI Overview summaries. Using a difference-in-differences design, we find that AI Overviews increase engagement in SFW communities: daily comments rise by 12.0 percent and the number of commenting users by 12.4 percent relative to NSFW communities. The effects are concentrated in experience-based discussions (opinions, advice, and personal experiences) rather than fact-based information. However, the subsequent introduction of Google AI Mode, which allows users to interact conversationally with the AI summary, largely eliminates these gains in experience-based content. These results suggest that the effects of AI search depend critically on interface design and content type.

Information Retrieval.title: A Study of Prior Case Retrieval Using Lexical, Semantic, and Rhetorical Role Information in Indian Legal Documents
Information Retrieval.summary: For retrieving prior cases in Indian legal judgments, the problem involves distinguishing relevant legal facts from mere lexical similarities because a prior case that shares a statute with the query judgment is not necessarily relevant. In this paper, we describe an empirical evaluation of three consecutive designs of retrieval systems for the IL PCR(Indian Legal Prior Case Retrieval) task. We demonstrate that the combination of the rhetorical roles (Fact, Ratio Of The Decision, Precedent, Argument, Statute) is better than either using individual roles or performing full text retrieval, that statute similarity is not discriminative, and that a legal entailment reranker with training data produced by an LLM is much worse in terms of official evaluation than its internal validation score. Two rankers, with excellent internal MRR up to 0.97, performed poorly in terms of official evaluation (MRR as low as 0.14). Thus, we propose a new design with query disjoint splitting and frozen validation fusion. The result is a four stage pipeline with Micro F1 0.2549, MRR 0.6081, and nDCG@10 0.4187.

Information Retrieval.title: Iterative Critique-Refine Framework for Enhancing LLM Personalization
Information Retrieval.summary: Personalized text generation requires models not only to produce coherent text but also to align with a target user's style, tone, and topical focus. Existing retrieval-augmented approaches such as LaMP and PGraphRAG enrich profiles with user and neighbor histories, but they stop at generation and often yield outputs that drift in tone, topic, or style. We present PerFine, a unified, training-free critique-refine framework that enhances personalization through iterative, profile-grounded feedback. In each iteration, an LLM generator produces a draft conditioned on the retrieved profile, and a critic LLM - also conditioned on the same profile - provides structured feedback on tone, vocabulary, sentence structure, and topicality. The generator then revises, while a novel knockout strategy retains the stronger draft across iterations. We further study additional inference-time strategies such as Best-of-N and Topic Extraction to balance quality and efficiency. Across Yelp, Goodreads, and Amazon datasets, PerFine consistently improves personalization over PGraphRAG, with G-Eval gains of +8.5-12%, steady improvements over 3-5 refinement iterations, and scalability with increasing critic size. These results highlight that post-hoc, profile-aware feedback offers a powerful paradigm for personalized LLM generation that is both training-free and model-agnostic.

Information Retrieval.title: Audit Before You Update: Recording Artifacts and the Limits of Bounded Model Updates in MIMIC-IV ICU Prediction
Information Retrieval.summary: Clinical prediction models in intensive care degrade as data shift, and regulators such as the FDA ask developers to specify bounded update protocols in advance. Evaluations of such protocols assume that apparent drift reflects clinical practice rather than changes in how the database records care. We test whether update strategies can be evaluated on unaudited ICU data, and whether a parameter-bounded update gives up accuracy or attribution stability relative to full fine-tuning once the data are audited. We audit MIMIC-IV 3.1 (2008-2022) for recording artifacts and define a cleaning protocol. On the cleaned cohort, a label-free classifier two-sample test gates updates across three eras. We compare a bounded update, which retrains only treatment-context and fusion parameters, with full fine-tuning for two model families and two targets under a pre-specified non-inferiority margin of 0.015 AUROC, and measure attribution stability against the source model. In 2020-2022 about half of ICU stays have no input or procedure-event records, and a vasopressor ItemID migration makes the 2017-2019 label rate appear to fall when it actually rises. On the cleaned cohort, the gate detects drift in every era, including in physiology-only features, with no false alarms on null data. Bounded updating is non-inferior or superior in 10 of 12 primary cells, but this depends on the target, the model family and learning-rate tuning, and adaptation gains over never updating are small. At a shared learning rate, bounded updates keep physiological attributions more stable in neural models, clearly for vasopressor and less clearly for intubation; with separately tuned rates, full updates are more stable. Audits should precede update evaluation, and the update boundary should be chosen per target.
Information Retrieval.comment: Major revision: Added dataset temporal-validity audit, multi-era drift gating, non-inferiority testing for bounded updates, and procedural evaluations of XAI attribution stability across varied tuning setups

Information Retrieval.title: Personalized LLM Recommendation with Semantic IDs: Autoregressive Beam Search vs. Multi-Token Prediction
Information Retrieval.summary: Large-scale personalization is shifting from embedding-table retrieval to LLM-based recommenders that generate the Semantic ID (SID) of the item to recommend, where each SID is a short sequence of discrete hierarchical content codes. A single instruction-tuned model can then unify retrieval, content understanding, and language, and recommend brand-new titles from their content alone using SID; then, how should the model generate the SID? Traditionally, models rely on a single language modeling head that generates tokens autoregressively, typically using constrained beam search. In contrast, an emerging body of work explores multi-token prediction (MTP), where dedicated heads predict all tokens in parallel, substantially reducing the decoding latency associated with beam search. We report an industry-scale, apples-to-apples comparison of these two generation paradigms: single-head autoregressive decoding vs. MTP. We introduce a new auxiliary ranking loss, defined over the joint SID score, to train the MTP objective. We evaluate the SID training objectives on both quality and training/inference cost, inside a multi-task LLM that jointly does personalized retrieval, content question-answering (QA), and instruction following over a large streaming-media catalog. Our experiments show single-head beam search consistently beats MTP on most product-critical metrics: ranking and content QA, and trains at roughly 2.6x lower dollar cost on Qwen3-8B scale; MTP wins only on raw inference throughput. Around this finding, we detail an efficient training and inference stack and report end-to-end gains over the previous non-SID baseline equipped with an auxiliary ranking head: +77% item cold-start ranking, +22% content-QA accuracy, +2.8x faster training, with language metric regression traced to SID vocabulary expansion. We address the language regression by reinforcement learning post training.

Information Retrieval.title: KhyontekAI at CheckThat! 2026: Multilingual Dense Retrieval and Cross-Encoder Reranking for Scientific Web Claims
Information Retrieval.summary: Scientific claims shared through social media platforms frequently reference research findings without explicitly linking to the corresponding scientific publications. Automatically retrieving the correct scientific source for such claims is a challenging multilingual retrieval problem involving semantic matching, paraphrasing, noisy social media text, and cross-domain language variation. In this work, we present a multilingual two-stage retrieval framework for CLEF 2026 CheckThat! Task 1 on Source Retrieval for Scientific Web Claims. Our system combines fine-tuned dense retrieval models with cross-encoder reranking for improving multilingual scientific document retrieval. We evaluate multiple transformer-based dense retrieval architectures including multilingual-E5, BGE, and Contriever under different metadata configurations. We further investigate multilingual joint training, retrieval depth analysis, metadata enrichment, and language balancing strategies for improving retrieval effectiveness. Experimental results demonstrate that metadata enrichment consistently improves retrieval effectiveness, while fine-tuned cross-encoder reranking provides additional gains in retrieval precision. Our final multilingual system achieves MRR@5 scores of 0.6222 for English, 0.5112 for German, and 0.6254 for French, with an overall average MRR@5 score of 0.5862.
Information Retrieval.comment: 14 pages, 1 figure, 9 tables. Author version of the paper published in CEUR Workshop Proceedings, Vol. 4283 (CLEF 2026 Working Notes, Jena, Germany)

Information Retrieval.title: Local Citation Recommendation Without Graph Signals
Information Retrieval.summary: Resolving correct citations can be a time-consuming task for research writers. We address local citation recommendation (LCR), where the goal is to retrieve appropriate references for a given sentence. Web tools generally depend on the existing citation graph, which may bias results toward citation count or more recent publications. LCR research using full paper texts has been limited by the lack of publicly available data. We present a new dataset, the Local Citation Recommendation Corpus (LCRC), containing 14,735 scientific statements derived from astrophysics review papers, each with one or more citation targets whose full text is accessible via API. Using this dataset we systematically compare retrieval methods and develop a citation recommendation system that avoids citation graph bias while achieving 8.0% improvement in Recall@25 and 6.9% improvement in NDCG@25 over dense retrieval baselines without model fine-tuning. To support reproducibility, we make our code and dataset publicly available.
Information Retrieval.comment: Accepted at WASP 2026, co-located with AACL-IJCNLP 2026. 16 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/adsabs/LCRC Code: https://github.com/benjaminb/citeline

Information Retrieval.title: QASP: Query-Adaptive Robust Vector Search Policy
Information Retrieval.summary: A fundamental challenge of vector search is achieving consistently high recall while minimizing computational costs. Fixed search parameters cause significant performance variance across queries, and conventional evaluation on average recall masks these per-query disparities. We introduce QASP (Query-Adaptive robust vector Search Policy), which predicts the complete recall progression curve per query via a single upfront supervised regression, from which a search policy is derived for any recall target; this avoids iterative model invocations during search or separate predictors per target. By predicting normalized recall values with scale-invariant features and pre-search inference, QASP generalizes across recall targets, index configurations, and datasets. Its fine-grained progress predictions further enable a lightweight reactive complement that adjusts search depth based on predicted-versus-observed deviations without additional inference. We prove that QASP requires a finite training sample independent of dataset size and dimensionality, that its loss exceeds the irreducible lower bound of any fixed policy by a vanishing margin, and that its data access savings over fixed probing grow exponentially in intrinsic dimensionality. Experimentally, QASP achieves significantly lower recall variance and deviation from target, higher query satisfaction rate, and scales to large data and hierarchical indices without retraining, achieving 99% recall with 80% less data access.

Information Retrieval.title: Retrievable Gradients: Continual Post-Training Without Cumulative Weight Drift
Information Retrieval.summary: Continual post-training enables models to absorb emerging knowledge after deployment, but repeatedly updating shared parameters can accumulate weight drift, potentially causing catastrophic forgetting and degrading general capabilities. Retrieval-augmented generation avoids such parameter drift, yet often lacks the depth of parametric knowledge integration. In this paper, we propose ReGrad (Retrievable Gradients), a new paradigm that treats gradients as retrievable units of knowledge. ReGrad pre-computes document-specific gradients offline, stores them in an indexed Gradient Bank, and retrieves only query-relevant gradients at inference time for temporary weight adaptation. However, raw language-modeling gradients are optimized for token-level document reconstruction rather than for query-driven knowledge use. We therefore introduce a bi-level meta-learning objective that reshapes document-derived gradients into generalizable adaptation signals for downstream tasks. Experiments across general and domain-specific settings show that \textsc{ReGrad} outperforms CPT and RAG baselines, enabling scalable and reversible parametric knowledge injection without accumulating weight drift.

Information Retrieval.title: UMM-RM: An Upcycle-and-Merge MoE Reward Model for Mitigating Reward Hacking
Information Retrieval.summary: Reward models (RMs) are critical to reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). However, policy models can exploit biases or spurious correlations in dense RMs, causing reward hacking: RM scores rise while alignment with human preferences deteriorates, especially under distribution shift. We propose UMM-RM (Upcycle-and-Merge MoE Reward Model), which copies the feed-forward layers of an SFT checkpoint to initialize shared and routed experts, then trains the model on preference data. The always-active shared expert captures instruction-agnostic preference signals, while routed experts model fine-grained preferences across instructions or tasks. The experts are then merged into a single dense RM using learnable weights, preserving the robustness and exploitation resistance of expert diversity without MoE or ensemble inference overhead. Across multiple base models and preference datasets, UMM-RM improves preference accuracy, reduces reward hacking during PPO training, and achieves more stable preference alignment than standard dense RMs.

Information Retrieval.title: DRNOISE: Benchmarking Deep Research Agents in Misleading Evidence Environments
Information Retrieval.summary: Deep research agents increasingly operate over the open web, where relevant records coexist with redundant summaries, outdated reports, and misleading documents. Existing evaluations offer limited insight into whether agents preserve sound evidential standards when an ordinary-looking false document is deliberately seeded into a searchable environment and offers a direct shortcut to a conflicting answer. We introduce DRNOISE, a 100-task benchmark for answer recovery under misleading evidence. Each task has a unique gold answer supported by two corroborating indirect record chains; the paired noisy condition adds one plausible document that states a conflicting answer directly. The benchmark spans ten families of evidence operations. Among models with strong clean-task performance in the shared agent framework, this single intervention causes 66--88 percentage-point accuracy drops. Trace analyses reveal a pattern of verification inertia: agents often retrieve truthful records yet defer to the answer-like document without adequately checking its claim against the underlying evidence. Generic verification prompts reduce but do not close this gap. The setting is especially relevant to open-web deployment, where plausible falsehoods arrive through ordinary-looking pages without explicit adversarial instructions. Reliable deep research therefore requires more than retrieval and citation; it requires active reconciliation of direct claims with record-level evidence.

Information Retrieval.title: Horizon Scans can be accelerated using novel information retrieval and artificial intelligence tools
Information Retrieval.summary:
Introduction: Horizon scanning in healthcare assesses early signals of innovation, crucial for timely adoption. Current horizon scanning faces challenges in efficient information retrieval and analysis, especially in grey literature, presenting a need for innovative tools.
  Methodology: This article introduces SCANAR and AIDOC, open-source Python-based tools designed to improve horizon scanning. SCANAR automates the retrieval and processing of news articles, using de-duplication and unsupervised relevancy ranking. AIDOC aids filtration by leveraging large language models and text embeddings for calculation of semantic similarity, to reorder data based on relevancy.
  Results: Twelve internal datasets from horizon scans and four external benchmarking datasets were used. SCANAR improved retrieval efficiency by automating processes previously dependent on manual labour. AIDOC displayed work-saving potential, achieving around 65% theoretic reduction in manual review efforts at 95% recall or 20% reduction when adding CMH, an existing open-source algorithm to make data-driven decisions on stopping screening early. Comparative analysis with benchmarking data showed AIDOC's performance was similar to existing systematic review automation tools, though performance varied depending on dataset characteristics.
  Conclusion: The validation indicates that SCANAR and AIDOC show potential to enhance horizon scanning efficiency by streamlining data retrieval and prioritisation. These tools may alleviate methodological limitations and allow broader, swifter horizon scans. Further studies are suggested to optimize these models and to design new workflows and validation processes that integrate large language models.

Information Retrieval.title: Rethinking Evidence Modeling: Context-Coupled Graph Learning for Multimodal Recommendation
Information Retrieval.summary: Multimodal graph recommendation integrates observed interactions with item images and text to learn user preferences. These inputs constitute Semantic-Behavioral Evidence (SBE). Many existing graph methods incorporate collaborative and multimodal semantic relations, yet their aggregation and state updates remain context-separated, limiting the continuous composition of preference evidence across layers and the joint use of multiple sources. To address this limitation, we propose CC-MGRec, a context-coupled graph learning method that organizes SBE within a common graph learning context for cross-relation modeling and compositional propagation. Its context-coupled multimodal graph integrates user-item collaborative relations and item-item semantic relations, coordinating their message scales through joint normalization. Recommendation-grounded semantic calibration uses training behavior to adjust semantic neighbor weights while preserving normalized collaborative propagation coefficients. Collaborative-semantic compositional propagation updates shared node states layer by layer to continuously compose collaborative and multimodal semantic evidence, implicitly forming Preference Evidence Chains (PECs), including collaborative-semantic and visual-textual PECs. Joint execution of relation messages on the same shared node states within each layer preserves propagation outputs while reducing intermediate output processing and fusion overhead. We provide theoretical analysis of the proposed mechanisms. Experiments on three Amazon datasets demonstrate improved recommendation quality and faster inference during graph propagation.

Information Retrieval.title: Pathwise Alignment for Collaborative Filtering: Bilateral Conditional Flow Regularization
Information Retrieval.summary: Collaborative filtering predicts user-item interactions from implicit feedback. We focus on matrix factorization (MF) trained with the Bayesian Personalized Ranking loss. This loss updates each user embedding only through that user's observed items and sampled negatives, so sparse feedback gives MF few constraints. To constrain each user through other users, we propose Pathwise Alignment for Collaborative Filtering (PACF), which trains MF with one network shared by all training pairs. At points between user and item embeddings, a flow matching term trains the network to predict the user-to-item step, reversed and scaled for sampled negatives. A trajectory consistency term pulls each user's predicted path to end at the observed item. Both terms update the embeddings, so the network is discarded after training, thereby maintaining the efficiency of MF at inference. We prove that a network with bounded sensitivity to its input point accurately fits users who share an item only if their embeddings are close, so these users constrain one another. Against eleven discriminative and generative baselines, PACF achieves the highest performance on all seven datasets. Its relative gains over MF are largest where feedback is sparsest. The shared network thus supplies the missing constraints through other users.

Information Retrieval.title: Federated Semantic Residuals for Multimodal Recommendation
Information Retrieval.summary: Federated Recommendation Systems (FedRSs) learn collaborative scores from interaction histories on device and rank items by them, so a higher score means a higher rank. Item text and images add semantic information that can reorder the list. Existing Federated Multimodal Recommenders (FedMRs) fuse this content into their models, which can obscure how content reorders the list. We therefore propose the SEmantic Residual Adapter (SERA), which keeps content out of an existing FedRS and adds semantic residual scores to its collaborative scores. Content can then lift an item above another only when its semantic residual score exceeds the other's by more than their collaborative score gap. This score grows with the item's content similarity to the user's interaction history and is capped at a residual bound. We prove that for any content, an item can enter the list only if its collaborative score is within twice this bound of the lowest one in the list. A larger bound lets content lift more items, including irrelevant ones, so the bound trades off how far content reaches against accuracy. With a validated bound, SERA improves all three FedRSs on all six datasets without adding personalized parameters. It outperforms FedMRs in most comparisons and lifts some FedRSs above centralized baselines.

Information Retrieval.title: Toward Explainability in Multimodal Recommendation
Information Retrieval.summary: Multimodal recommender systems effectively alleviate data sparsity and cold-start problems by integrating heterogeneous information, yet complex cross-modal representations and model decision-making processes also introduce new interpretability challenges. Despite the rapid growth of research on the interpretability of multimodal recommendation in recent years, relevant methods and evaluation criteria remain relatively fragmented, lacking a unified conceptual framework. To address this gap, this paper categorizes existing methods into modality explanation and post-hoc explanation based on the timing and manner of explanation generation, and further constructs a progressive system for each category. Building on this foundation, this paper synthesizes four categories of evaluation metrics from both objective quantitative and subjective perceptual perspectives, and reviews relevant datasets along the dimensions of application domain and data source. Through a comprehensive analysis of existing research, we further propose future research directions. This paper aims to establish a unified analytical perspective across multimodal representation, recommendation decision-making, and user preferences, providing a research foundation for building transparent and trustworthy multimodal recommender systems.

Information Retrieval.title: Decoupling Search from Reasoning: A Vendor-Agnostic Grounding Architecture for LLM Agents
Information Retrieval.summary: Production LLM agents increasingly depend on real-time search, yet native search grounding bundles retrieval policy, provider choice, evidence injection, cost, latency, and generation behavior behind a single model-provider boundary. This coupling makes grounding hard to inspect, tune, reuse, or port, and can trigger Search-Induced Verbosity that breaks strict output contracts. We present Decoupled Search Grounding (DSG), a vendor-agnostic boundary that moves grounding outside the reasoning model through an MCP-compatible gateway, exposing provider routing, source-aware context rendering, configured fallback, retrieval-depth control, and exact plus semantic caching as first-class controls. Across five frontier models on SimpleQA, FreshQA, and HotpotQA, native search leads on recency-sensitive FreshQA, but DSG exposes a stronger frontier when control matters: on SimpleQA it nearly matches native accuracy (86.1% vs. 87.7%) at 91% lower search cost, preserves concise answer contracts, and reaches a 99.4% warm-cache hit rate with 68% lower latency. Deployed as a shared production grounding layer for large-scale agentic workloads with interchangeable models, DSG matches native-search accuracy on an e-commerce query-understanding (QIU) workload while cutting search cost by over 98%. Real-time grounding is best treated as an optimizable interface boundary, not a fixed model feature.
Information Retrieval.comment: Accepted at the EMNLP 2026; 16 pages, 9 figure

Information Retrieval.title: Understanding ChatGPT Citations: Evidence from Production Web Search Across Model Generations
Information Retrieval.summary: Generative engines such as ChatGPT Web retrieve webpages to answer user queries, but only a subset are shown as citations. Understanding this retrieval-to-citation process is important for generative engine optimization (GEO), which aims to improve content visibility in generative-engine responses. However, prior studies mainly analyze final responses, leaving the internal execution process and its variation across model settings less understood. To this end, we conduct an observational study of four ChatGPT Web settings from ChatGPT 5.2 to 5.5, covering Instant and Thinking modes at the URL, hostname, and entity levels. We examine how ChatGPT rewrites queries, retrieves candidate webpages, and selects references. The Instant settings remain mostly single-round, while GPT-5.4 Thinking frequently performs multiple retrieval rounds. Across repeated runs, candidates retrieved more often are also more likely to be cited. We then evaluate Google Search and the OpenAI Responses API as external proxies. Responses API candidates provide broader coverage, while its citations more closely match sources cited by ChatGPT Web. Both proxies match ChatGPT Web better at the hostname and entity levels than at the exact-URL level. Even when combined, they recover only about one quarter of cited URLs. We further test whether these external signals remain predictive when combined. Within the external candidate set, a supervised model combining them reaches AUCs above 0.74 for GPT-5.3 and GPT-5.5 at all three levels. These findings suggest that GEO should distinguish retrieval visibility from citation visibility, account for rewritten queries and run-to-run variation, and consider hostname- and entity-level presence in addition to exact URLs. Differences across settings also suggest that GEO strategies should be re-evaluated when the deployed setting or serving environment changes.

Information Retrieval.title: Retrieving Complementary Evidence for Multi-Hop RAG with Semantic Gain Graphs
Information Retrieval.summary: Multi-hop retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) requires finding documents whose evidence is useful in combination. Query relevance and graph connectivity help locate related content, but neither directly measures the additional information one document contributes given another. We introduce SG$^2$RAG, a framework that represents this complementarity through semantic gain. Offline, a large language model assesses the relevant and nonredundant information contributed by one chunk given another within neighborhoods proposed by semantic similarity. These ordered assessments are aggregated into symmetric edge weights to construct a reusable Semantic Gain Graph. Online, controlled Personalized PageRank starts from query-relevant seeds and ranks complementary evidence beyond the initial retrieval set. Experiments on MuSiQue, 2Wiki, and HotpotQA with two language model backbones show that SG$^2$RAG achieves the best average EM, F1, and Recall@10 among the evaluated single-retrieval methods. Under identical candidate support and propagation, semantic gain improves average F1 and Recall@10 over similarity weighting by 4.08 and 4.31 points. Analyses of supporting documents and improvements in three iterative retrieval frameworks further support its effectiveness as a reusable retrieval component.

Multimedia.title: Toward Generative Video Communication: A Dual-Stream Digital Transmission Framework
